In my view, O unhappy—indeed, most unhappy—Jews, your hearts imitate the hardness of stones: neither are they restrained from the wickedness of their unbelief by the testimonies of the Law, nor softened to receive true faith by the authorities of the prophets. Thus you tend not as rational human beings toward true life, but, having lost reason, as brute animals toward eternal death, since you give no faith to so many utterly true testimonies of Law and prophets, testifying that Christ is the true Son of God and of the Virgin [Col. 0130C]; nor do you wish to cast the scandal of his cross from your hearts. But because, as I have said, you have until now presumed irreverently to resist the proclamations of truth, to your own condemnation, I urge you humbly and carefully to hear what the angel Gabriel above announced to Mary, ever virgin, the mother of our same Redeemer, about his birth and his powers. For even if you have hitherto refused to believe the words of the prophets, you cannot at all contradict the oracle of the angel Gabriel.

For he says: “Behold, you shall conceive in the womb and bear a Son, and you shall call his name Jesus. He shall be great and shall be called Son of the Most High.” Observe, O wretched ones, that by these words the angel Gabriel most plainly proclaims the Lord Jesus—that is, our Savior—as the true Son of [Col. 0130D] God the Father and the true Son of a human Mother. “Behold,” he says, “you shall conceive in the womb and bear a Son.” Acknowledge, O Jews, that Christ assumed the true substance of flesh from the true flesh of the Virgin. It follows: “He shall be great and shall be called Son of the Most High.” Truly great, of whom the Prophet joyfully foretold in the psalm: “Great is the Lord and exceedingly praiseworthy; and there is no end to his greatness” (Ps. 47). I wish you, O Jews, to answer my questions. Behold, you have heard that according to his humanity he assumed a natural bodily substance from the Virgin Mother. Say, then, who is that Most High whose son the Redeemer of the human race is said to be called? Beyond doubt he is the one whom the prophet, rejoicing and exulting with all his inmost being, praises in the psalm, saying: “I shall praise the Lord according to his righteousness, and I shall sing to the name of the Lord Most High” (Ps. 7). And again: “It is good to praise the Lord and to sing to your name, O Most High” (Ps. 91). And elsewhere: “You, Lord, are Most High over all the earth; you are exceedingly exalted above all gods” (Ps. 96). Thus, according to the testimony of the angel Gabriel, our Lord Jesus Christ is the Son of God the Father Most High, begotten by that same Father before all ages. Therefore, O Jews, believe him whom you deny even today with defiled mouth and obstinate heart to be true God from true God, and to be the Son ever coeternal with the eternal Father. But when it is said in the future tense, “He shall be great and shall be called Son of the Most High,” do not suppose [Col. 0131B] this means that our Lord Jesus Christ did not exist before the birth of Mary, ever virgin. Rather understand it as the venerable priest Bede says: the divine majesty’s power, which the Son of God possessed eternally, this same man, born in time, received, so that one person in two natures might be the mediator and redeemer.

Again, O Jews, that you may recognize yourselves defeated in all things, I urge you patiently to hear what the angel Gabriel adds concerning this same eternal King, Jesus Christ, for our instruction—indeed, for that of the whole Church: “And the Lord God shall give him the throne of David his father, and he shall reign over the house of Jacob for ever; and there shall be no end of his kingdom” (Luke 1). It is as though he said more plainly: He shall reign in the present, as true life dwelling in the hearts of his own by grace; and he shall reign in the future, calling his faithful ones from exile to glory. And as Isaiah says: “There shall be no end to the peace of his kingdom” (Isa. 9). Hence the exulting Psalmist said: “Blessed are those who dwell in your house, O Lord; for ever and ever they shall praise you” (Ps. 83). Beyond doubt these words of the angel Gabriel are sweeter to believers than honey and the honeycomb, and therefore should often be recalled. “The Lord God shall give him the throne of David his father,” that is, the Israelite people, to whom David and his sons supplied the governance of the temporal kingdom. This spiritual kingdom was given to Christ when God the Father ordained that he should be incarnate from David’s seed, so that he might call that people an everlasting [Col. 0131D] kingdom. And he shall reign not only over a single people of the Jews, but “he shall reign over the house of Jacob for ever,” that is, in the whole Church, which belongs to the lot of the patriarchs through faith in and confession of this same Lord Jesus Christ: both those born from the patriarchs’ line, and those cut from the wild olive—that is, born from the Gentiles—and grafted into the good olive, that is, received by grace into the adoption of the children of God. These words of the angel Gabriel, surely, are not to be consigned to forgetfulness but embraced with the affection of spiritual love. For these most sweet and true oracles of the heavenly messenger gladden the minds of those who hear them; and, recalled more and more, they produce in the hearts of believers a greater sweetness of eternal wisdom.

[Col. 0132A] Again, if you please, O Jews, let the angel’s testimony concerning Christ, stated above, be recalled, so that the hardness of your hearts may be somewhat softened to receive true faith. “And the Lord God,” he says, “shall give him the throne of David his father; and he shall reign over the house of Jacob for ever, and there shall be no end of his kingdom.” As stated above, “David’s throne” means the kingdom of the Israelite people, which David in his time governed with faithful devotion, at once by command and with the Lord’s sanction. Therefore God the Father gave our Lord Jesus Christ the throne of David his father when he ordained that he should be incarnate for us from David’s line, so that he might advance by spiritual grace to the eternal kingdom the people whom David ruled by temporal sovereignty. Of him the Apostle says: “He delivered [Col. 0132B] us from the power of darkness and transferred us into the kingdom of the Son of his love” (Col. 1). Hence also, instructed by divine inspiration, the same Jewish people, when that Son of God and the Virgin was hastening to Jerusalem to suffer for the salvation of the whole human race, joyfully sang in his praise: “Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord, the King of Israel” (John 12).

It follows: “And he shall reign over the house of Jacob for ever, and there shall be no end of his kingdom” (Luke 1). For our Redeemer Jesus Christ reigns in the house of Jacob, as stated above—that is, in the holy Church: namely, among those who drew their fleshly origin from the stock of the patriarchs, and among those who, born carnally from other nations, have been reborn in Christ by the spiritual washing [Col. 0132C]. In this house, that is, in the holy Church, he shall reign for ever. “And there shall be no end of his kingdom,” says the angel. For God and man, Jesus Christ, reigns in the house of Jacob—that is, in the Church of the present time—when, dwelling in the hearts of the elect through faith and love, he rules them and guides them by divine protection to receive the gifts of heavenly recompense. He will reign in the future, when, once the condition of temporal exile is finished, he brings those same people into the dwelling of the heavenly homeland. In that house, that is, in the heavenly homeland, continually refreshed by the sight of his presence, they rejoice to do nothing but devote themselves to his praises.

Meanwhile I urge you, O Jews, diligently and gladly to hear the words which the most blessed Mary, ever virgin, answered to the angel who announced them to her. I said “ever virgin” because she remained a virgin before childbirth, in childbirth, and after childbirth. For you too ought for this reason to love her with the highest affection and honor her with the greatest reverence: because she descended from Abraham’s line, bore the Son of almighty God, and remained inviolate after childbirth. If you understand this well and piously, you will plainly recognize what glory and honor she is to all your race after Christ. Beyond doubt God the Father chose this rose from David’s stock, from whom he willed that his most beloved Son should assume flesh for the salvation of the human race. Although this most holy Virgin drew her origin from royal descent, she nevertheless maintained in her conduct the highest degree of humility and innocence, and thus deserved without doubt to be exalted [Col. 0133A] above all women. But now, O Jews, let us hear together what this most holy Virgin, who had resolved to persevere throughout her life in virginity, answered when the angel announced that a son conceived by the Holy Spirit would be born to her. “How,” she said, “shall this be, since I do not know a man?” (*ibid.*). When Sarah laughed at God’s promise, and Mary said to the angel promising her a son, “How shall this be, since I do not know a man?”, why were they not made mute like Zacharias? Namely, because Sarah and Mary do not doubt that what is promised will be done, but ask how it will be done. Zacharias, however, who says that he does not know, says that he does not believe; he seeks another author for his faith, and therefore received the sign of silence, because signs are given not to believers but to unbelievers. It is therefore clear that the most blessed Virgin Mary believed that it would be done, since she asks how it would be done. “How shall this be, since I do not know a man?” It is as though she said more plainly: How shall it happen that I conceive, since I have resolved to remain in virginity? For she had read, and did not doubt, that a virgin would give birth. She also knew that what the angel announced had to be fulfilled; but because she had not read, nor heard from the angel, how it would be done or in what manner it ought to be fulfilled, she asks. For this mystery, hidden from the ages and not foretold by the prophets, was reserved for the angel; because the prophet Isaiah, who foretold that a virgin would conceive in the womb and bear a son, did not state more explicitly in what manner it would happen.

[Col. 0133C] At this point I urge you more earnestly, O Jews, not to be reluctant, but rather pleased, to hear what the angel Gabriel answered Mary, ever virgin, concerning Christ’s birth. Until now you have refused to hear the testimonies of the Law and Prophets, and thus have shown yourselves guilty before God and the Law. Therefore listen carefully to the angel’s testimony, and henceforth do not doubt that Christ is true God and true man. Certainly, although to your condemnation you have hitherto presumed to contradict the testimonies of the holy prophets, you can by no means contradict the testimony of the angel Gabriel. O foolish and evil people! Do you not know that, according to Solomon’s saying, “There is no wisdom, no knowledge, no prudence, no counsel against God” (Prov. 21)? Why, then, does earth and ashes grow proud [Col. 0133D] (Sir. 10)? For who are you, intoxicated with the venom of your fathers’ wickedness, that you contradict the Lord’s mouth and strive to overthrow his counsel, which he firmly decreed before all ages, without any retraction, to be accomplished—something you cannot possibly do? Since, therefore, you proudly resist God, “who calls things that are not as though they were” (Rom. 4), and with perverse boldness oppose his Holy Spirit, who through the mouths of holy prophets foretold from ages and generations that this birth of the Son of God and man, Jesus Christ, would take place, you are beyond doubt hastening not to life but to eternal condemnation. Finally I urge you reverently to hear what the heavenly messenger answered the most blessed Virgin Mary when she asked in what manner she would bear a son without a man’s embrace [Col. 0134A] and remain a virgin after childbirth. Henceforth recognize yourselves to be defeated in every respect, and do not presume further to resist so plain a truth.

“The Holy Spirit,” he says, “shall come upon you, and the power of the Most High shall overshadow you.” It should be noted that “Holy Spirit” is the name for every grace inspired by God. Therefore, coming upon the Virgin, the Holy Spirit cleansed her mind from the stain of vices, so that she might be worthy of heavenly childbirth; and by his operation alone created in her womb the holy and venerable body of our Redeemer—that is, with no male touch intervening, he formed sacred flesh from the flesh of the undefiled Virgin. But the power of the Most High shall overshadow blessed Mary, ever virgin, because the Holy Spirit filled her heart and restrained it from every heat of fleshly desire. He also cleansed her from temporal desires and consecrated together both her mind and body with heavenly gifts. It follows: “Therefore also that holy thing which shall be born of you shall be called the Son of God” (Luke 1). It is as though the heavenly messenger said more plainly: Since you shall conceive through the sanctification of the Holy Spirit, O Virgin Mary, what you bear will be holy, and you will not lose your virginity. All of us are conceived in iniquities and born in transgressions. But all who, by God’s gift, are foreordained to eternal life are reborn from water and the Holy Spirit. Our Redeemer alone, who deigned to be incarnate for us, was holy from the moment of his birth, because [Col. 0134C] he was conceived without iniquity.

We may indeed, in the words “and the power of the Most High will overshadow you,” understand something deeper concerning the mystery of the Lord’s incarnation, as the venerable Bede teaches. For we say that we are overshadowed when, beneath the blazing noonday sun, we place between ourselves and the sun a tree or some other sort of shelter, so as to make its heat or light more bearable for us. Our Redeemer, therefore, is rightly signified by the sun’s light or heat: he both illumines us with the knowledge of truth and kindles us with love for his sweetness. Hence he himself said through the prophet: “But for you who fear my name, the Sun of righteousness shall rise” (Mal. IV). The most blessed Virgin Mary received the rays of this sun [Col. 0134D] when she conceived the Lord. Yet this same Sun—that is, the divinity of our Redeemer—covered itself with the veil of human nature, as with a kind of shade, by whose mediation the Virgin’s womb could bear him. Thus the power of the Most High overshadowed her, when Christ’s divine power both filled her with its presence and clothed itself in the substance of our frailty, so that it might be contained by her.

Therefore God the Father, O Jews, gave our Lord Jesus Christ the throne of David his father; and he reigns in the house of Jacob, that is, in the holy Church, which, as has been said, belongs by faith in the same God and man Jesus Christ to the inheritance of the patriarchs—whether in those who drew their bodily origin from those patriarchs, or in us, who, though born bodily [Col. 0135A] from other nations, have been reborn in Christ through the spiritual washing. “For ever,” that is, both in the present exile and in heaven. True, therefore—indeed, most true—is the testimony which God the Father previously gave through the prophet Jeremiah concerning this same most beloved Son of his, saying: “A king shall reign, and he shall be wise; and he shall execute judgment and justice in the earth” (Jer. XXIII).

§ V.

Christ, king and son of the Virgin, is not only wise, but, more gloriously, is true Wisdom itself, whom God the Father begot from himself before all ages, through whom he created, sustains, and governs all things. Although Wisdom is to be called Son, not Daughter. The testimony of John and the beautiful testimony of Fulgentius are adduced. Solomon declares him not created but begotten. David finely testifies that Christ is true God and true man; from this the author concludes that the Jews are children of falsehood. Through the prophet Hosea he complains of them, recalling the mercy of the eternal Father and of Christ toward the Jews [Col. 0135B]. He adduces a saying from Deuteronomy for their rebuke. From the Book of Wisdom he sets forth their venomous thoughts and sacrilegious acts, which they maliciously devised against Christ. He commends the Book of Wisdom. He counsels them, although their predecessors have sunk into hell, to strive to attain eternal life, so that their old age may not be without honor.

I wish to know, O Jews, you who say that you know the books of the Old Testament, what you understand in those same books concerning the wisdom of this eternal King. I urge you not to be ashamed to bring forward publicly what you have read about him in those books, so that, having recognized the truth which he himself is, you may faithfully deserve to worship him with God the Father and the Holy Spirit, together with us, as one true God. Yet you must first know that the sacred writings of the Old Testament [Col. 0135C] are to be understood not literally but spiritually. “For the letter kills, but the Spirit gives life” (II Cor. III). Moreover, you must know that, while you observe the Law carnally, you cannot understand it spiritually at all. It also greatly harms your ability to understand the Old Testament spiritually that the perversity of malice and wickedness possesses your minds. For how can you speak good things when you are evil? Hence Solomon too says: “Wisdom will not enter a malevolent soul, nor dwell in a body subject to sins” (Wis. I).

[Note: [Col. 0135] Interpreters frequently observe that the Book of Wisdom is designated by many with the name of Solomon.]

Therefore hold it as certain that, unless you first cast out from your hearts the stony hardness of unbelief and, renewed through the womb of the sacred font, believe that the holy Trinity—namely Father, Son, and Holy Spirit—is one natural and true God, you will by no means be able spiritually to understand the books of the Old Testament. But because partly through ignorance, partly through malice, and partly through obstinate unbelief, you lack the knowledge of spiritual understanding—or rather, what is more serious, have lost it through sins that deserve this—I, through God’s grace preceding, following, and accompanying me, shall gladly expound to you, according to the authority of Catholic writers and to whatever extent I can, the meanings of the holy Scriptures of the Old and New Testament, so that, abandoning the faithlessness of Jewish superstition, you may believe Christ to be true God [Col. 0136A] and true man, and may deserve with the children of the Church to belong to the inheritance of the elect.

Let us therefore recall once more the aforesaid testimony of God the Father, which he previously gave through the prophet Jeremiah concerning Jesus Christ his Son, in order to show you, O Jews, defeated in every respect: “A king shall reign,” he says, “and he shall be wise” (Jer. XXIII). Truly this King is a wise King—indeed, most wise—because he is the Wisdom of God the Father, who speaks of herself in the Proverbs of Solomon: “I came forth from the mouth of the Most High, firstborn before every creature” (Ecclus. XXIV). “I,” she says, “Wisdom, dwell in counsel and am present in learned thoughts. Mine are counsel and equity; mine is prudence, [Col. 0136B] mine is strength. With me are riches and glory, splendid wealth and righteousness. My fruit is better than gold and precious stone, and my offspring than choice silver. I walk in the ways of righteousness, in the midst of the paths of judgment, that I may enrich those who love me and fill their treasuries. The Lord possessed me at the beginning of his ways, before he made anything from the beginning. From eternity I was established, and from ancient times, before the earth was made. The abysses did not yet exist, and I had already been conceived; the springs of waters had not yet burst forth; the mountains had not yet stood in their massive weight; before the hills I was brought forth. He had not yet made the earth, the rivers, or the poles of the world. When he prepared the heavens, I was present; when he enclosed the abysses with a fixed law and circle; when he established the upper regions on high and balanced the springs [Col. 0136C] of waters; when he set its boundary around the sea and gave the waters a law, that they should not pass beyond their bounds; when he weighed out the foundations of the earth, I was with him, ordering all things; and I delighted day by day, playing before him at all times. Playing, I say, in the world of the earth; and my delights were to be with the children of men” (Prov. VIII).

If, therefore, O Jews, you apply your hearts diligently to what has been said, you will recognize openly and without any ambiguity that this King, namely the Son of God and of the Virgin, is not only wise, but, more gloriously, is himself true Wisdom, whom God the Father begot from himself before all ages, and through whom he created, sustains, and governs all things. Of angels, as St. Isidore says in the first book of the *Sentences* [Col. 0136D] (ch. 10), it was said: “Wisdom was created before all things” (Ecclus. I). But the Wisdom of God the Father, who is Christ, was not created, but ineffably begotten from God the Father before the foundation of the world; through him, the Creator and ruler of all ages created all things from nothing. Of this eternal Wisdom, who was not created but eternally begotten, who is Christ, Jesus son of Sirach of Jerusalem, grandson of Jesus the high priest, says at the beginning of his book, which we call *Ecclesiasticus*: “All wisdom is from the Lord God, and has always been with him, and is before the age” (Ecclus. I). And shortly afterward: “Who has investigated the wisdom of God [Col. 0137A] that precedes all things?” (ibid.). And again: “To whom has the root of wisdom been revealed, and who has known her subtleties?” (ibid.). For neither a human being on earth nor an angel in heaven can fully know how the root of wisdom, preceding all things, which is Christ, was begotten from God the Father before all ages. For with God the Father and the Holy Spirit he penetrates, contains, and governs all things. For in her, as is read in the Book of Wisdom (ch. VII), is “a spirit of understanding: holy, unique, manifold, subtle, mobile, distinct, undefiled, certain, gentle, loving what is good, keen, permitting nothing that is good to be hindered, humane, kindly, steadfast, secure, possessing every power, overseeing all things, and comprehending all spirits, intelligible, pure. [Col. 0137B] For wisdom is more mobile than all things that move, and reaches everywhere because of her purity. For she is a vapor of the power of God and a pure emanation of the glory of almighty God; therefore nothing defiled comes into her. For she is the brightness of eternal light, the spotless mirror of God’s majesty, and the image of his goodness. Though one, she can do all things; remaining in herself, she renews all things; and, passing through nations into holy souls, she makes friends of God and prophets.”

What do you say to these things, O Jews? What do you answer to what has been said? Since so many most truthful witnesses agree beyond doubt with one another, so many authorities of the Old and New Testaments truly concur with one another, and so many proclamations of apostles and evangelists [Col. 0137C] firmly assert that Christ is true God and true man, has unbelief been altogether expelled from your hearts? Or, still hindered by the blindness of your long-standing malice, do you intend stubbornly to resist the truth, which is Christ? Surely it is long since you ought, having been overcome by so many most true disputations and convicted by so many authoritative arguments, to have expelled from your hearts the superstition of Jewish observance, which you have recognized as having long ago received its end in Christ, and to have believed Christ to be true God and true man, without whom you can in no way attain to God the Father. I do not wish you, O Jews, so readily to consign to oblivion what this most wise King, namely the Son of God and of the Virgin, [Col. 0137D] said above concerning himself in the Proverbs of Solomon: “I came forth from the mouth of the Most High, firstborn before every creature” (ibid.). Christ, therefore, is by nature the Wisdom of God the Father, and came forth as firstborn before every creature from the mouth of his same most high Father, through whom God the Father himself created all things from nothing. Perhaps you say, O Jews: if Christ is the Wisdom of God, why is he called Son and not Daughter? To this we answer that he is called Son and not Daughter for two reasons: first, because the name Son is more honorable than Daughter; second, because he deigned to be born from the Virgin not in the person of a daughter but in the person of a Son.

These most true and most sweet words of the Son of God, therefore, must be repeated again and again, to confirm our faith and overcome your [Col. 0138A] adamantine faithlessness, O Jews. “I came forth,” he says, “from the mouth of the Most High, firstborn before every creature.” Attend carefully, O Jews, lest you depart empty from this most holy and profound reading. Thus, when the Wisdom of God, who is Christ, says that he comes forth from the mouth of the Most High, he shows that he is by nature of one and the same substance with the Father. When he adds, “firstborn before every creature,” he demonstrates that he was with God the Father from eternity, and that he is not created but creative. St. John the Evangelist also affirms this at the beginning of his discourse concerning Christ, who truly is the Wisdom of God, saying: “In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God.” [Col. 0138B] (John I). That is, more plainly: Christ, the Son of God, was in the beginning—that is, in God the Father, who is beginning without beginning—the Word; and that Word was with that same God his Father, who begot him from himself; and the Word was God. And the two, namely God the Father and God the Word, were not two gods, but by nature one true God. “This was in the beginning with God. All things were made through him, and without him nothing was made.”

It is most manifest, O Jews, that this Word, who was in the beginning, was with God, was God, and through whom God the Father made all things, and without whom nothing was made, is not a creature, as you irreverently say, but the Creator. Therefore listen carefully, O Jews, to the words of truth, so that, believing Christ, who [Col. 0138C] is most true truth, to be naturally one God with God the Father and the Holy Spirit, you may attain eternal joys. Believe with complete certainty, therefore, that God the Father neither created nor made this Word, but begot him from his own natural essence, through whom he created all things from nothing. God the Father could not have created all things through him if he were a creature. But if perhaps you are unwilling to assent to my salutary counsels, at least listen to St. Fulgentius, a bishop distinguished for wisdom and holiness, an exemplar of good works, established in Christ’s Church; and receive with a kindly, not a stubborn, mind his testimony concerning the eternity of the Word, who is Christ.

“It is,” he says, “the Word whom God the Father [Col. 0138D] begot from himself from eternity—not as something uttered and then absent, but as one who remains begotten; not transitory, but eternal; not made by the eternal Father, but begotten; not only begotten, but also only-begotten. For God the Father, as has been said, begot one Word from himself, through whom he created all things from nothing. Therefore, in that God the Father made all things through that Word, it is shown that he did not make the Word but begot him. That Word, therefore, is God from God, Creator from the Creator; whence he has in himself by nature what the Father is. Thus the Son, God, was born from the Father, God: other in person, not different in nature. Therefore the Son is always with the Father, always from the Father, always in the Father; always with the Father, with whom he has one natural immensity; always with the Father [Col. 0139A], with whom he has one natural eternity; always from the Father, from whom he has an eternal nativity by nature; always in the Father, with whom he has one divinity naturally equal.”

Meanwhile I urge you, O Jews, not to hear this most true testimony concerning Christ’s eternity and divinity, set forth by St. Fulgentius, negligently or sluggishly while sleeping in the malice of your minds; but, watchfully, believingly, and lovingly, store it more attentively in your hearts for your salvation. Therefore, as has been said above, the Son is always in the Father, God in God. He who is Father is indeed other; he who is Son is other. Yet neither is another God, because Father and Son are one God. Accordingly, when speech arises concerning God the Father and God the Son, we rightly say that the Father is one [Col. 0139B] and the Son another; and nevertheless we rightly say that Father and Son are one God. For when we say that the Father is one and the Son another, we show the distinct persons of Begetter and Begotten; but when we say that Father and Son are one God, we show the one nature of undivided divinity itself. The person of the Begetter, therefore, is other than that of the Begotten; but the nature of Begetter and Begotten is one.

I do not wish you, O Jews, readily to consign to oblivion what you have heard from St. Fulgentius teaching concerning Christ’s eternity and divinity; rather, retain it continually for your instruction. For he says: “God the Father begot one Word from himself, through whom he created all things from nothing.” And he added: “That Word, God from God, is Creator from the Creator. Thus the Son, God, was born [Col. 0139C] from the Father, God: other in person, not different in nature. He is also always with the Father, always with the Father.” St. John the Evangelist also testifies to this, saying: “In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God” (John I).

What do you say to this? What do you answer, O Jews? What objection do you raise? Behold how truly the witnesses of truth agree with one another. Behold how effectively they refute the false arguments of your disputation, strengthen the Catholic faith by most true testimonies, and demonstrate that the claim of your objection is futile. They bring forward most true testimonies from the books of the Old and New Testaments, by which they show beyond doubt [Col. 0139D] that you are children of falsehood; they confirm in every way the faith of the Catholic Church, and utterly overthrow the faithlessness of your superstition, O Jews. With polluted mouth and faithless heart you say, O unhappy Jews, that Christ was not begotten by God the Father, but created. But he who truly is the Wisdom of God the Father testifies concerning himself, saying: “I came forth from the mouth of the Most High, firstborn before every creature” (Ecclus. XIV). Note carefully that he did not say “created first,” but “firstborn before every creature.” It is therefore manifest that Wisdom, whom God the Father did not create from some other material or among the other creatures, but begot from himself before every creature, is not created but creative. This the Son of God himself, who truly is this Wisdom of God the Father of whom we speak, [Col. 0140A] testifies in the same Proverbs, saying: “When God weighed out the foundations of the earth, I was with him, ordering all things; and I delighted day by day, playing before him at all times” (Prov. VIII). Since the Wisdom of God, who is Christ—not made or created, but begotten before every creature—says that she orders all things with God the Father, that is, creates and arranges them, and plays before him at all times, it is beyond doubt clear that she is not created but created all things with God the Father.

The testimony of God the Father also proves, O unhappy Jews, that you have lied in your opposition, when through the Psalmist he praises Christ, whom you assert to be not Creator but creature, as true God and true man, saying: “My heart has uttered [Col. 0140B] a good word; I speak my works to the King” (Ps. XLIV). By these words God the Father commends Christ according to both natures, and first according to the divine, saying: “My heart has uttered a good word.” Lest we suppose that God the Father needed marriage for the begetting of his Son, he shows us that this begetting was accomplished not from another, but from himself, saying: “My heart,” that is, my innermost substance and all my hidden mystery, “has uttered,” that is, begotten, “a good Word,” namely one equal and consubstantial with me. “My heart has uttered a good word.” It is as though he said: I did not beget it through an external union, but from my heart, just as a man generates counsel from his heart: before what he is about to do exists, it is counsel. But the Son is the Father’s counsel, whom he begot from himself before every [Col. 0140C] creature. And this is the sense: “My heart has uttered a word”—that is, from my fullness and hidden essence I begot the Word, namely the Son who is called Word because through him the Father is made known to the world. This Word is also called good, because the Son of God alone, with the Father and Holy Spirit, is good in his nature. Hence he himself says in the Gospel: “No one is good except God alone” (Luke XVIII). This Word is also good because through him all good things, and nothing evil, were made. It follows: “I speak my works to the King.” That is, more plainly: I speak, that is, I bring forth the Word. He says here the same thing that he said before, but adds, “my works to the King,” where he says that all God’s works are in the Word itself. Hence John the Evangelist says that “what was made,” [Col. 0140D] namely in time, “was life in him” (John I), so that there may be nothing in the work which was not first in counsel. It is as though he says openly: “I speak my works to the King,” that is, I eternally beget the Word, with whom and in whom I order all things before they exist in actuality. God the Father also calls this same Word his tongue, saying: “My tongue is the pen of a scribe writing swiftly” (Ps. XLIV). It is as though he said: Not only do I order all things with him, but I also speak through him, because he is my tongue and also my pen. For as a scribe does nothing without a pen, nor a pen without a scribe, so Father and Son work together. Observe that he compares the Word not to a passing sound, but to writing, which remains, in order to show that the Son is coeternal with God the Father. “Of a scribe,” I say, “writing swiftly,” because God the Father ordered not one thing after another, but all things together in one eternal Word.

[Col. 0141A] Behold how openly we prove by so many most true authorities of the holy Scriptures that you, O wretched and pitiable Jews, are defeated in your objection and have lied in every respect, you who said that Christ was not begotten of God the Father before all ages but created in time. Therefore, with the Holy Spirit teaching them, the witnesses of truth agree with one another and, as we said above, prove beyond doubt that you are children of falsehood. We rightly call you children of falsehood, because we prove you false in every respect. How are you not children of falsehood, when you neither observe the Law nor receive the Gospel? I marvel, moreover, why you boast that you are sons of Abraham, when you have degenerated from that most holy [Col. 0141B] patriarch. With what face do you call yourselves his sons, when you do not hold his faith—indeed, more damnably, deny it by blaspheming? As St. Isidore says, he was the first worshipper of the holy Trinity; therefore God made him the father of many nations through faith. If then, O foolish and malicious Jews, you truly wish to be sons of Abraham, hold the faith of Abraham, so that through this life you may deserve to rest in his bosom. Each person is called the son of the one whose teaching he follows. Therefore you who do not hold the faith of the holy Trinity which Abraham held are not Abraham’s sons but sons of the devil. How are you not of the devil as father, when you blasphemously deny that the three persons whom Abraham confessed [Col. 0141C] by faith and works are the divine essence? It is plainly evident that you are heading toward eternal death without any intervening delay, since you deny Christ, who with the Father and Holy Spirit is true life. Hence he himself, through the prophet Hosea, justly complains to us, who embrace him with the arms of faith and with most ardent love of charity, concerning you, saying: “Woe to them, because they have departed from me; they shall be laid waste, because they have transgressed against me. I redeemed them, and they spoke falsehood against me . . . . I instructed them and strengthened their arms; and they devised evil against me. They turned back so as to be without a yoke; they became like a deceitful bow” (Hos. VII).

Unless, therefore, O Jews, you receive with devout mind the faith which is in Christ [Col. 0141D] Jesus, there will be for you in this present age woe, that is, manifold tribulation, and in the age to come eternal damnation. Therefore, you who departed from him by worshipping idols, I urge to draw near to him faithfully by believing in him. Do you not see, O wretched people, that what he threatened you has now been fulfilled? Have you not already been laid waste from king to beggar, expelled with great disgrace from the land of promise, scattered throughout all regions under heaven, and indeed, what is more serious, made subject to slavery among all nations throughout the world? For thus that most just Judge said to you: “They shall be laid waste.” Why, Lord Jesus Christ, shall the Jews whom you brought out of Egypt and settled, to serve your name, in the land which you promised to their fathers, be laid waste? [Col. 0142A] Namely because they departed from me by worshipping idols and transgressed against me by worshipping golden and silver calves and breaking my covenant, by which [Note: [Col. 0141D] Another manuscript: “to whom.”] I said: “You shall not make for yourselves strange gods, nor worship them” (Exod. XX). It is as though Jesus Christ, God and man, said more plainly: Truly, I redeemed them from Egypt and delivered them from the hands of the most powerful kings who opposed them on the way, and from many tribulations; I brought them into an excellent land, and they spoke lies against me, saying: “We have no king but Caesar” (John XIX). And again: “You bear witness concerning yourself; your testimony is not true” (John [Col. 0142B] VIII). It follows: “And I instructed them,” namely through Moses and Aaron and the other prophets of truth taught by the Holy Spirit, so that they might believe, fear, and love me as one natural and true God with God the Father and the Holy Spirit; do good and depart from evil; do to others what they would have done to themselves, and not inflict on others what they would not wish inflicted on themselves; and, when the fullness of time came, might confidently [Col. 0142C] hope that I would be born of a Virgin for the salvation of the human race, die on the cross for the redemption of the world, descend into hell to free the righteous who were in punishments, rise again on the third day, ascend into heaven, sit at the right hand of God the Father, and at the end of the world come thence to judge the living and the dead. All these things I taught them through the Law and the prophets. I also strengthened their arms through my Gospel, promising them eternal joys, the fellowship of angels, and the vision of God almighty, my Father who is in heaven—things which had not been promised them through the Law and the prophets. O Christ, lover of all goodness and innocence! While you recount the many benefits which you piously and mercifully bestowed upon the Jews, you praise the mercy of God the Father and your own mercy, announce their future and just condemnation unless they repent, and thereby strengthen us more firmly in your faith and love. But amid these things, O highest Emperor of kings, author and lover of peace, Christ, most generous rewarder of your servants, if it pleases your [Col. 0142D] most holy kindness, we wish to hear how, after so many benefits, the Jews glorified God the Father and you, or what thanks they rendered. “They gave no thanks,” he says, “but, what is graver and more condemnatory for them, devised evil against me; incited by it, they cried out to Pilate, saying: ‘Away, away, crucify him; for if you release this man, you are not Caesar’s friend’” (John XIX). To them fittingly applies what David had foretold much earlier in the Psalms: “They thought and spoke wickedness; they spoke iniquity on high” (Ps. LXXII). Again, concerning these same most deceitful Jews, the Son of God and the Virgin [Col. 0143A] adds through the same prophet, saying: “They turned back so as to be without a yoke; they became like a deceitful bow” (Hos. VII). That is, more plainly, Jesus Christ, God and man, complaining of them to us his faithful people, says: It was not enough for them that they devised evil against me and urgently asked Pilate to crucify me; they also returned to what they had been before I called and instructed them, so as to be without the yoke of my knowledge and love. Concerning this I frequently said in the Gospel: “Take my yoke upon you and learn from me, because I am meek and humble of heart, and you shall find rest for your souls” (Matt. XI). And again [Note: [Col. 0143D] Another manuscript: “It follows.”]: “My yoke is sweet and my burden light” (ibid.). [Note: [Col. 0143D] Another manuscript: “It follows.”] It is as though he said: After my preaching they returned, like a dog to its vomit, to their former perversity [Col. 0143B], so as to be without the yoke of my knowledge; and they became like a deceitful bow. It should be observed that a deceitful bow wounds the one who holds it and shoots arrows from it. Thus the Jews, like a deceitful bow, wounded with the arrows of their tongues me who redeemed and instructed them and strengthened their arms, saying to Pilate: “His blood be upon us and upon our children” (Matt. XXVII). And again: “If this man were not an evildoer, we would not have handed him over to you” (John XVIII).

O Jewish nation, blind nation, O wicked and perverse nation! Is this what you render to the Lord for all the good things he bestowed on you, O foolish and senseless people? (Deut. XXXII). Is he not your spiritual father, who possessed you from the beginning, made you from nothing, and, with none of your merits preceding, made and created you because of his goodness? O faithless nation, remember the days of the ancient fathers, consider each [Col. 0143C] generation, and you will clearly recognize that he is by nature the Son of God and of the Virgin, to whom you inflicted the aforesaid and many other injuries. Ask your father, and he will tell you (ibid.) that he is the one who led Abraham out from Ur of the Chaldeans, delivered his race from Egyptian slavery, and, after the enemies had been slain, settled it in the land of the Canaanites. Why, then, have you forsaken God your maker and departed from God your savior? Why, O most unhappy nation of all nations, have you provoked him through strange gods and stirred him to anger through many abominations? You sacrificed to demons and not to him—to gods, that is, whom you did not know, indeed whom you made by your own design [Col. 0143D] and industry. Therefore, O faithless nation, you forsook the God who begot you; and, what you cannot deny, you forgot the Lord your Creator when you delivered the Son of God and of the Virgin, through whom God the Father created all things and without whom nothing was made, into the hands of the Gentiles to be crucified. How do you say, O unhappy Jews, that you have not forgotten the Lord your Creator, when you not only despised to hear the preaching of his most beloved Son, sent specially by him to gather the lost sheep of the house of Israel (Matt. X), but also, through your persuasion and petition, delivered him over most cruelly to death? How have you not forsaken God your maker [Col. 0144A], when you denied the very King of angels, through whom God the Father governs and rules all things in heaven and on earth, by despising him and inflicting innumerable injuries upon him; and publicly professed Caesar, a man devoted to idolatry, as your king? Truly you are unhappy—indeed, most unhappy—you who refused to receive with the highest honor and reverence the Son coeternal and consubstantial with God the Father as the God and Lord of your fathers, namely Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob; but, producing false witnesses and accusing him with insolent cries, condemned him as guilty without cause to death, and chose as your king a man who rendered worship to idols.

I do not wish you to be ignorant, O Jews, that the ancient malice which stirred the minds of your fathers to persecute Christ today closes the eyes of your minds against contemplating the truth, which is Christ. The impiety which they conceived against Christ at envy’s instigation they carried out through wicked deeds. The Book of Wisdom, speaking in their person, most plainly declares their venomous thoughts, deceitful machinations, and sacrilegious acts [Col. 0144B] which they maliciously devised “against the Lord and against his Christ” (Ps. II), saying: “Let us entrap the righteous man,” that is, Christ, unjustly, “because he is useless to us and opposed to our works; he reproaches us with the sins against the Law and defames us for the sins against our discipline. He promises that he has knowledge of God and calls himself the Son of God. He has become a contradiction of our thoughts [Col. 0144C]. He is burdensome even to behold, because his life is unlike that of others and his ways are changed. We are considered by him as trifles” (Wis. II).

“Nugae” [“trifles”], as St. Isidore says [Note: [Col. 0144D] Book X of the *Etymologies*, under the letter N], is a Hebrew word. For we find this term explained thus where the Lord says through the prophet Zephaniah: “I will gather the *nugae*, those who had departed from the Law” (Zeph. III). From this we may know that the Hebrew language is the mother of all languages, because it openly explains what it says. It follows: “And he abstains from our ways as from impurities, and prefers the latter end of the righteous, and boasts that he has God for his father. Let us therefore see whether his words are true, and test what will happen to him, and we shall know what his latter end will be. For if he is the true Son of God, he will receive him and deliver him from the hands of his enemies. Let us question him with insults and torture, so that we may know his reverence and test his patience. Let us condemn him to a most shameful death; for, according to his words, there will be regard for him.” [Col. 0144D]

Listen more attentively, O brood of vipers, to what the Book of Wisdom says concerning your law-transgressing and murderous fathers. “They thought,” it says, “these things aforesaid and went astray.” Why? “Because their own malice blinded them, and they did not know the mysteries of God; nor did they hope for the reward of righteousness, nor judge that there was honor for holy souls.”

[Col. 0145A] I want you to know, O Jews, that the aforesaid book is called *Wisdom* because it proclaims therein the coming of Christ, who is the Wisdom of God the Father, and clearly sets forth his Passion. Meanwhile, I admonish you, O Jews, carefully to consider the aforesaid testimony from the Book of Wisdom, so that you may understand what you ought to avoid and what you ought to follow. It says above concerning your foolish fathers, who repaid Christ evil for good and, indeed, fastened him to the cross without cause: “They thought these things and went astray, for their wickedness blinded them” (Wis. 2).

In what thoughts did they go astray? Was it in thinking good things? By no means. Rather, because they denied Christ, who is truly King of heaven and earth, saying, “We have no king but Caesar” (John 19), therefore [Col. 0145B] they strayed from the way of truth, which is Christ, and incurred eternal condemnation. Why? “Because their wickedness blinded them.” Truly, the eye of the mind cannot behold the light of truth, which is Christ, when it is closed by the dust of wickedness. Since, therefore, they conceived wickedness against Christ in their hearts, they lost the light of wisdom, which is Christ.

What do you observe in these matters, O Jews? Certainly, if you wish to imitate your fathers, who publicly denied Christ, you will never be able to attain the joys of eternal life. If you follow the crooked footsteps of your parents, you will in no way be able [Col. 0145C] to contemplate the light of truth and wisdom, which is Christ. “If a blind man offers guidance to a blind man, both fall into a pit” (Matt. 15). You must therefore by every means, O Jews, avoid the pit of eternal condemnation into which you see your unbelieving forefathers have fallen.

Let, then, their eternal condemnation, which they incurred through the error of unbelief, be your correction. Let their eternal punishment draw you back from the deadly perfidy of your unbelief. Let their perpetual disgrace be a safeguard for your salvation. This, then, is my counsel: as your unhappy parents descended into hell through the error of unbelief, so may you strive, by good works and by faith in the most holy Trinity—namely, Father, Son, and Holy Spirit—to ascend into heaven. Therefore, “lay hold of instruction, lest you perish from the righteous way” [Col. 0145D] (Ps. 2), together with your murderous and sacrilegious fathers.

If you receive the discipline of the Church’s religion and faithfully believe in and love the Wisdom of God the Father, which is Christ, you may obtain forgiveness of sins. But if you choose to persist in your wickedness and do not receive the instruction that brings your salvation, you will perish without doubt. Hence it is read in the Book of Wisdom: “Wretched is he who rejects wisdom and instruction; their hope is empty, their labours without fruit, and their works useless” [Note: [Col. 0145] Manuscript: “uninhabitable.”]. “But the ungodly shall receive punishment according to the evil thoughts they conceived: they who neglected [Col. 0146A] the Just One”—that is, the Son of God and of the Virgin, “who committed no sin, neither was deceit found in his mouth” (Isa. 53)—“and departed from the Lord,” that is, from the worship of the whole Trinity. “But the children of those adulterers”—namely, those who departed from God the Father and the Holy Spirit and served idols—“shall come to their end, and the offspring of their unlawful bed shall be destroyed. And even if they live long, they shall be counted as nothing, and dishonoured shall be the end of their old age” (Wis. 3).

§ VI.—

Chastity is praised in the New Testament, where it took its beginning in the undefiled Virgin; thus, through love for Jesus Christ her spouse, the generation of mother Church is beautiful and chaste. He exhorts them to believe without any doubt that Christ is the Wisdom of God the Father, since he continually and devoutly calls them to the worship of God. By Solomon’s testimony he highly commends acquiring him in the same terms, since knowledge of him is eternal life. He further asks why they cut the Book of Wisdom away from the prophetic books.

These things stated above [Note: [Col. 0145] Another manuscript here inserts words from the preceding sermon.], O Jews, were foretold in the Book of Wisdom concerning those who neglected the Just One—that is, who despised Christ, the Son of God and of the Virgin—and who departed wickedly from him who, together with God the Father and the Holy Spirit, is one true God by nature: by denying him, blaspheming him, inflicting upon him innumerable injuries, and living wickedly.

Hear also, O Jews, what the same Book of Wisdom says concerning those who received Christ with a devout and faithful mind: “The fruit of good labours is glorious, and the root of wisdom [Col. 0146C] does not fail” (Wis. 3). And again: “O how beautiful is a chaste generation with charity! For its memory is immortal, because it is known both with God and among men” (Wis. 4).

These words, certainly, are spoken concerning the children of the Church. For chastity is praised not in the Old Testament but in the New. In the Old Testament, barren women who could not have children called themselves unhappy. Thus, in Genesis, we read that Rachel said to Jacob her husband: “Give me children, or else I shall die” (Gen. 30). Hannah also, Samuel’s mother, complained to Eli the priest because she had no son, saying: “My lord, I am a woman exceedingly unhappy” (1 Kings 1). Elizabeth likewise, mother of St John [Col. 0146D] the Baptist, who remained barren until old age, when she knew that she had conceived rejoiced thus in the Lord, saying: “For thus has the Lord dealt with me in the days in which he looked upon me, to take away my reproach among men” (Luke 1).

Therefore this holy woman, who had long lived barren, rejoiced at the gift of offspring because she was free from the reproach of barrenness. It is clear, then, as we said above, that in the Old Testament it was a reproach for women not to have children; but in the New, it is a glory for virgins and for those who restrain themselves in chastity for God’s sake. Children, indeed, are the reward of marriage, for whose sake marriages themselves are celebrated.

Thus the beautiful and chaste generation is the children of the Church, renewed through baptism and washed from sins in love of God and neighbour. They are rightly called a beautiful and chaste generation because, made white through the womb of the sacred font and strengthened in faith in the holy Trinity, they are found in the love of their Creator not only chaste but also virgins. Hence holy mother Church is called chaste and a virgin, because she does not commit fornication with idols or foreign gods, but through charity keeps her faith incorrupt and undefiled for Jesus Christ, her spouse.

Accordingly, as Blessed Augustine says (*Sermon 12, On Time*), where the flesh is not untouched by intercourse, let the conscience be virginal in faith in Christ. And lest you doubt, O Jews, that what we say is so, hear what Solomon says, in the person of Christ, in the Song of spiritual love concerning this same beautiful and chaste generation of holy Church: [Col. 0147B] “You are wholly beautiful, my beloved, and there is no stain in you” (Song 4).

I want you to know, O Jews, that holy Church together with all her children is one Church and one body, and Christ is her head. Let us therefore hear what Jesus Christ, the heavenly spouse, says about her beauty and chastity. “You are wholly beautiful,” he says, “my beloved, and there is no stain in you.” Since it is written, “No one lives without sin, not even an infant whose life upon earth is but one day” (Job 14, according to the Septuagint), what does it mean that the bride is called wholly beautiful, with no stain found in her? Elsewhere, indeed, it is written: “The stars are not clean in the sight [Col. 0147C] of God” (Job 25). And elsewhere: “For we all offend in many things” (James 3). And the Apostle John says: “If we say that we have no sin, we deceive ourselves, and the truth is not in us” (1 John 1). Again he says: “If we say that we have not sinned, we lie, and do not do the truth” (ibid.).

But while holy Church in her children cleanses herself from daily sins through penance, while each day she washes away venial sins with tears and withdraws herself from grave sins, although she sins frequently, she nevertheless continually preserves her purity through continual repentance. Hence it is said to the order of bishops in the Apocalypse: “Blessed is he who keeps his garments, lest he walk naked and the shame of his nakedness be seen” (Rev. 16). Therefore Solomon also says in the book which we call Ecclesiastes: [Col. 0147D] “Let your garments be white at all times, and let oil not fail from your head” (Eccl. 9). And: “But my righteous one lives by faith” (Hab. 2; Rom. 1; Gal. 3).

Although, therefore, as soon as he sins he departs from righteousness, nevertheless, so long as he continually believes in him who justifies the ungodly and continually bewails his sins under faith in him, he retains his righteousness through continual tears and other good works.

It should be noted that this beauty—namely, the chastity and virginity of the generation of holy Church—took its beginning in the New Testament from the most blessed ever-Virgin Mary, who is the head of virgins. She is [Col. 0148A] the queen and originator of virgins; she is the mother of our head, who is the Virgin’s Son and the spouse of virgins. From her come companies of holy men and maidens; from her come male and female followers of perpetual continence, making themselves chaste not only in body but also in mind itself, castrating the root of desire, practising a heavenly and angelic life amid earthly mortality, and retaining perpetual incorruption in corruptible flesh. Before them all fruitfulness of the flesh and all marital chastity yield place.

For since the whole universal Church herself is a virgin betrothed to one husband, as the Apostle said (2 Cor. 11), how much more worthy are those of her members who preserve even in the flesh what the whole Church preserves in faith? Yet virginity should be praised in such a way [Col. 0148B] that marriage is not condemned. Therefore, as Blessed Isidore says [Note: [Col. 0147] Book II, *On Ecclesiastical Offices*, chapter 18, from which all these things have been taken.], one must not condemn what is good—namely, marriage—but recommend what is better, namely continence or virginity.

You heard above, O Jews, on the testimony of the Book of Wisdom, that those who denied Christ and did not wish him to reign over them “shall be counted as nothing, and dishonoured shall be the end of their old age.” You also heard in the reading of the same Book of Wisdom how beautiful is the chaste generation of holy mother Church through love for Jesus Christ, her spouse. Convicted, then, in your objection by so many most true testimonies, overcome by so many authorities of the Old and New Testament, what remains except that, believing Christ to be one true God by nature together with God the Father and the Holy Spirit, [Col. 0148C] you should endeavour as quickly as possible to be cleansed by his baptism?

If you humbly receive my counsel, you will be able to recover the grace of God the almighty Father, which you lost by denying his most beloved Son. Therefore, with all diligence I exhort you and with all earnestness admonish you to believe that this Son of God and of the Virgin is true God and the natural Wisdom of God the Father, without whom you cannot at all attain salvation for your souls.

For this true Wisdom of God the Father, which is Christ, has always called you to the worship of God: formerly in the Old Testament through the Law and the prophets, as it were secretly; but now, in this age of grace, through apostles, bishops, and [Col. 0148D] the other preachers of the Church, he invites you publicly, no longer secretly, to the true faith. Hence Solomon says in the Book of Proverbs: “Wisdom,” that is, Christ, “preaches abroad, raises her voice in the streets, cries aloud at the head of the crowds, and utters her words at the gates of the city, saying: ‘How long, little ones, will you love childhood?’” (Prov. 8).

It should be noted that “little ones” sometimes means those in childhood, and sometimes those of small understanding. The Hebrew people, certainly, before entering the promised land, were as an infant, because they had not been instructed either by the precepts of the Law or by the oracles of the prophets. To them Moses said: “The Lord your God will carry you as far as [Col. 0149A] this place, as a woman is accustomed to carry her infant” (Deut. 1). For the Law was a pedagogue to the Jews, as though they were little children.

But let us hear what the Wisdom of God the Father says: “How long, little ones, will you love childhood?” As though Jesus Christ, God and man, in whom truly are all the treasures of the wisdom and knowledge of God the Father, said more plainly: O Jews, who are little ones in knowledge of me, how long will you love childhood? That is, the carnal observance of the Law, which long ago, when you were still little children, small in the love of God, I taught you in the wilderness, and in my coming wished you to have faith. “For the Law and the prophets prophesied until John” (Matt. 11).

But I, the new man, came into the world, and at my coming changed all the carnal ceremonies of the old Law and gave new precepts to the world. Why then, O foolish Jews, do you not desire the eternal joys that would profit you if you rightly believed in me, but lust after earthly and transitory things that harm you? Why, O senseless ones, who read in the Law and the prophets that I was to come, do you not merely refuse to receive me now that I have come, but even hold my knowledge in hatred?

Again, this same natural Wisdom of God the Father, which is Christ, mercifully exhorts you, O Jews, in the same Book of Proverbs to faith and love of himself, saying: “Turn to my correction, and I will pour out my spirit to you and make my words known” (Prov. 1). As though he said more plainly: Because I first called you—that is, proclaimed my coming through the Law and the prophets, and then through my Gospel—and you refused to come faithfully to me; because I stretched out my hands to perform miracles and also spread them out upon the cross for the redemption of you and of the whole world, and there was no one who would look; moreover, you despised all my counsel, by which I intended to adopt you as sons and daughters; and you, in pride and blasphemy, drove my disciples, after subjecting them to insults and beatings, out of your borders, and neglected my rebukes, by which I wished, as a father does his children, to call you back to the way of truth—yet at least now, though late, turn to my most health-giving correction, and I will pour out my spirit upon you, namely the spirit of understanding and godliness; and I will also [Col. 0149D] show you my words, which without doubt “are spirit and life” (John 6).

You have heard, O unhappy Jews, how devoutly the Wisdom of God the Father, which is Christ, calls you to himself, that you may believe him to be one God by nature with the same Father and the Holy Spirit. How gently he reproves you, so that you may promptly repent of evils done; and how mercifully, desiring to adopt you as his sons, he promises you the Holy Spirit, that, enlightened by him, you may grow more perfectly in knowledge and love. For he, as Blessed Paul says, “wills all people to be saved and to come to the knowledge of the truth” (1 Tim. 2).

“Think of him with goodness, and seek him in simplicity of heart; for he is found by those who do not put him to the test, and appears [Col. 0150A] to those who have faith in him” (Wis. 1). Seek him, therefore, O Jews, as Solomon says, in simplicity of heart, and believe him to be naturally the Son of God the Father, so that you may find him and have him propitious in the day of need. “He appears,” he says, “to those who have faith in him.” Truly, the Son of God and of the Virgin appears in the present life through faith to those who truly believe in him and love him with their whole heart; and he will appear in the future by sight.

Therefore I admonish you, O Jews, to seek this Wisdom, which is Christ, with the utmost earnestness, and, once found, faithfully to love him, so that, instructed by his teaching, you may be made blessed with the children of the Church. Solomon speaks thus in praise of him in Proverbs: “Blessed is the man who finds wisdom,” namely that which is Christ, “and who abounds in prudence. Its acquisition is better than the trade of silver and gold, and its fruits are first and most pure. It is more precious than all wealth, and nothing that is desired can be compared with it. Length of days is in its right hand, and riches and glory in its left. Its ways are beautiful ways, and all its paths are peaceful. It is a tree of life to those who lay hold of it, and whoever holds it shall be blessed. The Lord”—namely God the Father—“founded the earth by this wisdom,” which is Christ; “he established the heavens by prudence,” for Christ is the wisdom and prudence of God the Father. “By his wisdom the depths burst forth, and the clouds grow dense with dew” (Prov. 3).

You know, O Jews, that whoever hates wisdom [Col. 0150C] hates his own soul, and whoever loves it loves life. Hence the Wisdom of God the Father itself, which is Christ, says in Proverbs: “All who hate me love death” (Prov. 8). And again: “He who sins against me harms his own soul” (ibid.). Therefore hear instruction with your ears, lay hold of it by your works, and do not cast it away in pride of mind.

Let us also hear what this Wisdom of God the Father itself says of itself for the instruction of us all: “Blessed is the man who hears me, who watches daily at my doors, and keeps guard at the posts of my gateway” (ibid.). And again: “He who finds me finds life and draws salvation from the Lord” (ibid.). Solomon shows in the same Book of Proverbs how mercifully and with what fullness of charitable affection this Wisdom of God the Father, which is Christ, invites all to faith and love [Col. 0150D] of himself, saying: “Does not wisdom cry aloud, and prudence raise her voice? Standing upon the highest and loftiest heights beside the road, in the midst of the paths, beside the gates of the city, at the very entrances, she speaks, saying: ‘O men, to you I cry, and my voice is to the children of men’” (ibid.).

O Jews, perhaps we might have passed along the temporal road in ignorance of this Wisdom, if that same Wisdom had stood in corners of the path—that is, in a hidden place. But it is said to have stood not in corners but in the midst of the roads. This Wisdom of God the Father would indeed have needed to be sought out had it wished to remain hidden; but after it publicly displayed the mysteries of its Incarnation, after it furnished an example of humility to the proud, it placed itself in the middle of the paths before you, as before travellers: so that, if we do not wish to seek it, we may stumble into it unwillingly; and, though we neglected to see it, we may touch it as it shows itself.

But let us hear what this Wisdom of God the Father, which is Christ, says: “Receive my instruction, and not money; choose doctrine rather than gold” (ibid.). As though he said openly: Receive my instruction, which teaches you to love God in all things and above all things, to love your neighbour as yourself, to despise money, seek heavenly things, avoid sins, and acquire virtues. It follows: “Choose my teaching rather than gold.” As though he said: Choose my evangelical teaching rather than gold, for through it you can acquire knowledge and love of your Creator. Hence Solomon also says in Proverbs: “Possess wisdom, for it is better than gold; acquire prudence, for it is more precious than silver” (Prov. 16).

Concerning this uncreated Wisdom also, which is Christ, hear, O Jews, what is read in the Book of Wisdom: “I desired, and understanding was given to me; I called upon God, and the spirit of wisdom came into me. I preferred her to kingdoms and thrones, and considered riches as nothing in comparison with her. I did not compare any precious stone to her, since all gold in comparison with her is little sand, and silver shall be regarded as mud in her sight. I loved her above health, beauty, and every loveliness, and resolved [Col. 0151C] to have her as my light, for her light is inextinguishable” (Wis. 7).

Therefore love above all things this Wisdom of God the Father, which is Christ, in comparison with whom all things become worthless; and believe him to be one true God with God the Father and the Holy Spirit, if you wish to attain eternal life. For knowledge of the supreme and undivided Trinity is eternal life, without which no one can live eternally. Hence Jesus Christ himself, God and man, speaks to God the Father, saying: “This is eternal life: that they may know you, the only true God, and Jesus Christ whom you have sent” (John 17).

Therefore resolve with faithful devotion to have this Wisdom of God the Father, which is Christ, as your light, so that, when the darkness of unbelief has been driven out, you may be able, with her as guide, to attain the homeland of eternal brightness. In this pilgrimage she illumines holy Church by evangelical teachings; remaining eternally in God the Father, from whom she has never departed, she illumines the holy angels in heaven.

It is proved that Solomon wrote the Book of Wisdom, in which are found such very clear testimonies concerning Christ’s coming, by those passages which are read there: “You,” he says, “chose me as king over your people and judge of your sons and daughters; and you told me to build a temple upon [Col. 0152A] your holy mountain and, in the city of your dwelling”—namely Jerusalem—“an altar, a likeness of your tabernacle, which you prepared from the beginning” (Wis. 9). And again: “Wisdom shall guide me soberly in my works, shall guard me in her power; my works shall be acceptable, I shall govern your people justly, and shall be worthy of my father’s throne” (ibid.).

[Note: [Col. 0151D] Among the Greeks the Book of Wisdom bears the title *Wisdom of Solomon*, because of the words cited here. Among the Latins, as we have already noted at folio 119, it bore the same title until the Roman council under Pope Gelasius or Pope Hormisdas [Col. 0152D]. It was believed to be Solomon’s insofar as it contains his thoughts, not his words and composition. Indeed, Jerome says: “The style of this book has the flavour of Greek eloquence.”]

These testimonies make it plainly understood that Solomon wrote the Book of Wisdom. This Book of Wisdom, as a certain wise man recalls, the Hebrews received among the canonical Scriptures. But after they seized and killed Christ, recalling the very clear testimonies concerning Christ in that same book, which say: “The ungodly said among themselves: ‘Let us unjustly seize the Just One, because he is useless to us and contrary [Col. 0152B] to our works; and he promises that he has the knowledge of God and calls himself the Son of God’” (Wis. 2); and below: “‘For if he is the Son of God, he will receive him and deliver him from the hands of his adversaries’” (ibid.); and then: “‘Let us know,’ they say, ‘his reverence and test his patience; let us condemn him to a most shameful death’” (ibid.)—for this reason, after taking counsel together, lest our people reproach them for so open a sacrilege, they cut the same book away from the prophetic volumes and forbade its reading among their own.

You heard, O Jews, that your parents received the Book of Wisdom among the canonical Scriptures before Christ’s coming, but after his Passion cut it away from the prophetic volumes and forbade its reading among their own. Why did they do this? Why did they reject, cutting from the canon of holy books, a book written by God’s wisdom and providence? Did they do this because of love and affection for Christ’s name? Rather, they did it out of hatred and ill will.

For if they had truly loved Christ, they would not have cast the Book of Wisdom—which openly proclaimed the Passion that they themselves had formerly inflicted upon him—out of the catalogue of divine Scriptures, but would have held it in the highest reverence. If they had believed Christ to be true God and true man, they would never have cut from the number of ancient books the sacred Scripture which had long before foretold his coming and clearly displayed the Passion carried out by them.

What do you observe in these matters, O Jews? What do you say or answer? Did not the Book of Wisdom bear witness to Christ when it openly proclaimed Christ’s coming and clearly showed the Passion inflicted on him by the Jews? And when your own unhappy parents cut that Book of Wisdom from the number of divine books because it plainly displayed Christ’s Passion, they undoubtedly bore witness to Christ: they grieved that the Passion which they knew they had committed themselves should be known and read by posterity [Col. 0153A]. Thus the Jews cut the Book of Wisdom from the canon of holy Scriptures so that, as has been said, our people might not reproach them for so open a sacrilege. But how great is human wickedness against the goodness and omnipotence of God! Since, therefore, they wickedly attempted to erase from the number of holy books the Book of Wisdom, which God the Father dictated through the Holy Spirit, as he did the other holy Scriptures, for the praise and glory of his name, and in which he clearly prefigured the coming and Passion of his most beloved Son, they acted ruinously against the salvation of their souls.

At this point I call you to account, O Jews, that you may tell me for what reason you presumed so proudly to oppose the dispensation and ordinance of almighty God. Why did you dare to overthrow his counsel? Why did you presume to cut from the canon of holy books the Book of Wisdom, which he who “calls those things which are not as though they were” ordered to be written for the instruction of his Church? What madness compelled you? What malice provoked you? What pride armed you against God and your Creator to such a degree that you wished to alter and wholly conceal a decree firmly established by him before all ages, and strove by every means, if it were possible, to prevent its fulfilment?

You fastened without cause to the cross the Son of God and of the Virgin, sent from heaven by God the Father for the salvation of the human race; and beyond this [Col. 0153C] you attempted to blot out the things written concerning him at the dictation of the Holy Spirit. From this it is understood that you have always acted contentiously against the Lord, and therefore lost your place and nation. I have already told you at length above, O unhappy ones, that “there is no prudence, knowledge, wisdom, or counsel against God” (Prov. 21). Therefore he who strives to overthrow God’s counsel tends not toward life but toward eternal condemnation. Whoever resists the divine dispensation provokes against himself from heaven the wrath of that same divinity. He goes against himself when he goes against God; striking at heaven, he falls into the deep; striving upwards, he falls from on high.

Return, therefore, O unhappy Jews, to your heart, and no longer wish to oppose the divine dispensation. It is not to your advantage to render God’s work void, even if you could do so: that work which he firmly ordained before all ages to be fulfilled in its time for the salvation of the human race. “What can clay say against the potter?” (Isa. 45). Or how can the vessel formed say to the potter: “You did not make me well”? Therefore willingly receive my profitable counsel, and do not any longer oppose the divine dispensation.

What do you observe in these matters, O Jews? What do you say? What do you answer to the things stated above? I think you are now so thoroughly defeated that you ought never again to mutter against the Wisdom of God, which is Christ, nor offer any further resistance at all [Col. 0154A]. Therefore believe that the Lord Jesus Christ—whom you have until now denied by saying that he was not begotten by God the Father before all ages, but took his beginning in time from Mary, his mother—is one true God with the Father and the Holy Spirit, containing all things, ruling all things, and reigning through infinite ages of ages.

For God the Father begot him from himself before all ages; as has often been said, he mercifully sent him for the redemption of the human race through the womb of the undefiled Virgin Mary. He made all these things known from the beginning of the world through figures, declared them through oracles, taught them through teachers of the Law, foretold them through the prophets, and finally made them more openly manifest to the whole world through [Col. 0154B] the evangelists and apostles.

[Note: [Col. 0153D] Another manuscript here begins the eighth sermon on the Lord’s Nativity, omitting the words that link it with what precedes: “For him indeed”; but we follow [Col. 0154D] the order of our own manuscript.]

Blessed Job, foreseeing in the Spirit these teachers also of the New Testament, who were to explain openly the hidden darkness of allegories in the Old Testament and bring them into light by preaching, said concerning the Lord: “He searched out also the depths of rivers and brought hidden things into light” (Job 28). Explaining this, Blessed Gregory says [Note: [Col. 0154D] Book XVIII of the *Exposition of the Morals*, chapter 21.]:

> “For what else are ‘rivers’ here called but the sayings of the ancient Fathers? Who can sufficiently weigh what a mighty river burst forth from the breast of Moses while he established the Law? What a mighty river flowed from the heart of David? How abundant were the streams that issued from the work [Note: [Col. 0154D] Printed edition: “from the mouth of Solomon.”] of Solomon and from the rivers of all the prophets?
>
> “But of these rivers, O unhappy Jews, you possess the outward appearance, since by preserving the surface of the letter you remain ignorant of their depths. We, however, since the Lord came in the flesh, seek in these same rivers—that is, in the Scriptures of the holy Fathers of the Old Testament—their inward spiritual meaning, and investigate their depths and mysteries. The Lord himself is said to do this because, by his gift, we are able to do it. Therefore through us, who follow not ‘the letter which kills’ but ‘the spirit which gives life’ (2 Cor. 3), the Lord searches out the depths of rivers and brings hidden things into light, because spiritual exposition now illumines the words of the Law which a history exceedingly dark obscures.
>
> “Thus Truth, speaking in parables through the Gospel, commands his disciples: ‘What [Col. 0154D] I tell you in darkness, speak in the light; and what you hear in the ear, preach upon the housetops’ (Matt. 10). For the plainly spoken words of interpreters have made the sayings of the ancient Fathers so evident to us. Hence the prophet Isaiah, beholding the plain words of holy Church’s exposition, no longer obscured by the darkness of allegories, cried out: ‘A place of rivers, broad and open streams’ (Isa. 33).”

Understand at this point, O Jews, “that the sayings of the Old Testament were like narrow and enclosed streams, which compressed the immense meanings of their knowledge into a most obscure compactness.
