It is therefore manifest, O Jews, that, just as Noah and those with him could not be saved from the flood’s danger except through the ark, so the human race could by no means be delivered from the bondage of the ancient enemy and everlasting destruction except through baptism and the sacraments of Christ’s Passion and Resurrection. If, then, you wish to escape eternal damnation and reach the heavenly homeland with the Church’s children, you must [Col. 0228D] believe that the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit are one true God, and receive baptism in his name for the remission of sins with the utmost devotion. Know therefore certainly, and do not doubt at all, O Jews, that unless you believe and are baptized, you cannot be saved (Mark XVI).

So that you may no longer doubt that Christ is true God, but firmly believe him, O Jews, to be the true Son of God, I urge you again patiently to hear how the patriarch Noah prefigured that same Jesus Christ, God and man, suffering and crucified for humanity’s salvation and shamelessly mocked by your fathers. [Note: [Col. 0228D] Isidore, chap. 8.] Noah, then, [Col. 0229A] after the flood planted a vineyard; drinking wine from it, he became drunk and lay naked in his tent (Gen. IX). Christ became drunk when he suffered for our sins. He was stripped naked when he was crucified in his tent—that is, in the midst of his people. Ham, seeing the nakedness of his father Noah, mocked him. So too the Jews, seeing Christ’s death, derided him, saying: “He saved others; himself he cannot save” (Matt. XXVII).

But Shem and Japheth, knowing of their father’s nakedness, placed garments upon their backs and, entering backward, covered their father’s nakedness. Shem and Japheth are the two peoples believing in Christ from circumcision and uncircumcision. Knowing their father’s nakedness—that is, seeing the Savior’s Passion—they placed their garments, namely, recalled the sacraments of the Scriptures, and covered their father’s nakedness—that is, honoured Christ’s Passion. For a garment signifies a sacrament, while the back is the memory of things past, because the Church celebrates Christ’s Passion as accomplished, not as still awaiting fulfilment. For we cover Christ’s Passion with a veil when we honour it by a sacrament.

Shem, the first brother, signified the holy apostles and those who first believed from among the Jews. Japheth, however, the last brother, represented those who would believe from the Gentiles and those Jews who, near the end of the world, are to be converted to Christ through the preaching of Enoch and Elijah. But when the middle [Col. 0229C] brother—that is, the impious Jewish people, called middle because it neither held the primacy of the apostles nor believed last among the Gentiles—saw his father’s nakedness, this meant that it consented to the death of the Lord and Savior; and it told his brothers outside, because through the Jews themselves what had been secret in prophecy was made manifest.

Thus Ham became the servant of his brothers, as you, O Jews, are to this day servants of Christians. You carry the Law and the Prophets, but understand what you read carnally; therefore you can by no means attain the most true Truth, which is Christ. But we gladly read the writings of the Law and the Prophets; and because in them we seek not a carnal but a spiritual sense, we openly find in those same holy Scriptures of the Old and New Testaments Jesus Christ, Son of God and of the Virgin, foretold, born, suffering, raised again, and exalted at the right hand of God the Father.

Meanwhile, I urge you, O Jews, gladly to hear how happily these two brothers who reverently covered their father’s nakedness are blessed by their father: “Blessed be the Lord of Shem; let Canaan be his servant. May God enlarge Japheth, and may he dwell in the tents of Shem” (Gen. IX). Shem is the elder by birth, from whom were descended the fathers—that is, the patriarchs, prophets, and apostles. [Col. 0230A] Japheth, however, is the father of the Gentiles, from whom the holy Church was gathered to Christ. This *Japheth* is interpreted “breadth.” Ham, the middle son, whose name is interpreted “hot,” being, as it were, set apart from both, neither remaining in Israel’s first fruits nor in the fullness of the Gentiles, signifies not only unbelieving Jews but also heretics hot not with the spirit of wisdom but with impatience, who customarily disturb the peace of the saints by their heresy.

Or, alternatively: [Note: [Col. 0229D] From “Ham” down to “is called” are also the words of Isidore, but from book VII, chapter 6 of the *Etymologies*; consult Grial there [Col. 0230D] and the passage from Jerome which he cites.] Ham was surnamed “hot” from a foreknowledge of the future. For his descendants possess that region of the earth which is hotter because it lies near the sun. Hence Egypt is called *Cham* in the Egyptian language even today. Ham, therefore, was cursed in his son, as in his fruit—that is, in his work. Hence his son Canaan too is fittingly interpreted “their motion”; and what else is that than their work? Japheth dwells in the tents of Shem because the holy Church will be justified in the house of the Law and the Prophets. That Ham’s descendants were condemned when he sinned signifies that the Jewish people, who crucified Jesus Christ, God and man, passed on the just penalty of its condemnation to its children, saying: “His blood be upon us and upon our children” (Matt. XXVII).

Clearly, then, O Jews, you are cursed with Ham, Noah’s son, because you did not reverently [Col. 0230C] cover the nakedness—that is, the Passion—of your Father, namely Jesus Christ, God and man, which he mercifully endured for your salvation and that of the whole world. That is, you did not honour it by faithful belief, but mocked it with insults and reproaches. But Shem and Japheth—that is, the Christian peoples—are blessed by God. Seeing the nakedness, that is, the Passion and death, of Jesus Christ their Redeemer, they do not mock him with reproaches as scourged, crucified, dead, and buried; rather, they reverence and adore him with the utmost devotion as now truly raised and seated at the right hand of God the Father, and believe him to be one true God with God the Father and the Holy Spirit.

Therefore, because you, O Jews, despised him by mocking him, you have been handed over into captivity to those same Christian peoples throughout the world. If, then, you wish to be freed from temporal and [Col. 0230D] eternal bondage and, with Japheth—that is, with the Christian people—to be enlarged in the tents of Shem, that is, in the faith of the patriarchs and prophets, who most clearly foreshadowed and most truly foretold that Christ was to come for the redemption of the world as true God and true man, you must believe without hesitation that he was sent by God the Father and has already redeemed the world. For Japheth—that is, the Christian people—is enlarged in the tents of Shem when it understands spiritually the deeds of the patriarchs and the sayings of the prophets. By this means it strengthens and unassailably fortifies the catholic faith by the authorities of the Old Testament.

But if, O Jews, you are not yet confirmed in the catholic faith by so many corresponding figures of the patriarchs and so many prophetical oracles that most openly agree in declaring Christ true God and true man, but doubt still remains in your minds, [Note: [Col. 0231D] “Hear here,” or something similar, must be supplied for the sense of the sentence to stand.] consider how clearly Isaac prefigured the Son of God and the Virgin suffering for the redemption of humankind: when his father Abraham, having bound his hands and feet, placed him by the Lord’s command upon the altar’s platform atop the pile of wood, took up the sword, and lifted his hand with the sword in order to sacrifice him.

Let us therefore, O Jews, if you please, call to mind the history of that time, and carefully examine together how Isaac prefigured Jesus Christ, sent by God the Father and offered to that same God the Father for the world’s redemption. For God said to Abraham: “Take your only son Isaac, whom you love, and go to the land of vision; there you shall offer him as a holocaust upon one of the mountains which I shall show you.” Therefore Abraham, rising in the night, saddled his ass, taking with him two young servants and Isaac his son. And he said to his servants: “Wait here with the ass. The boy and I will hasten yonder, and after we have worshipped, we shall return to you” (Gen. XXII). [Note: [Col. 0231D] Isidore, *Questions on Genesis*, chap. 18.]

Abraham, then, as has been said, is commanded to sacrifice his son Isaac. Obeying God, he saddled the ass, laid on the wood, left his servants with the ass far away, climbed the mountain alone with his son, and reached the place on the third day. Before Isaac arrived at the place of sacrifice, he himself carried the wood on which he was to be sacrificed. Then Abraham, armed with a sword and already nearly striking, was warned to spare him; yet he did not depart without sacrifice or without bloodshed. A ram appeared, caught by its horns in brambles; it was sacrificed, and the sacrifice was completed.

For Abraham is interpreted “exalted father.” Who, then, as has been said, was figured in Abraham by that sacrifice except God the exalted Father? Who in Isaac except Christ? For as Abraham offered his only and beloved son to God as a victim, so God the Father handed over his only-begotten Son to suffering for us. And as Isaac carried the wood upon which he was [Col. 0231D] to be laid, so Christ bore upon his shoulders the wood of his cross, on which he was to be crucified.

You have heard, O Jews, how openly Jesus Christ, God and man—whom you have hitherto denied in faithless heart and blasphemed with polluted mouth—was prefigured in the deeds of the holy patriarchs; and how humbly obedient he was to God the Father even unto death, and how much he suffered for the redemption of humankind according to the humanity which he received without sin from the incorrupt Virgin. Hear [Col. 0232A] also how openly, in this same history, the malice of your hearts and the hardness of your unbelief were prefigured.

I therefore urge you, O Jews, silently to hear what Abraham said to his two servants: “Wait here with the ass. The boy and I will hasten yonder, and after we have worshipped, we shall return to you.” The two servants of Abraham, left on the road with the ass and not brought to the place of sacrifice, prefigured you, O foolish Jews, who lived in servile fashion with your mother Hagar—that is, with the Synagogue—under the Law, and understood the Law and Prophets not spiritually but carnally. Therefore you did not approach the place of sacrifice—that is, you did not attain the salvation of your souls through Christ’s Passion. For those reach the place of sacrifice who understand Christ’s Passion as foretold in the Law and Prophets, and firmly believe it not still future but already long ago accomplished for the world’s redemption.

Why, then, did Abraham’s two servants remain far from the place of sacrifice with the ass—that is, with stupidity and blindness of mind—except because you, O foolish and blind Jews, were to be divided into two parts, depart from God, and serve idols? For in the ass your stupidity and recalcitrance are aptly understood, by which you always rebelled against divine commands. Although you knew God, you nevertheless abandoned him by despising him and bestowed upon idols the worship due to him; for this reason you were handed over to bondage under all nations beneath heaven. Moses, foreseeing this in the Spirit and speaking of the future as though it were already past, said: “The beloved grew fat and rebelled; he grew fat, thick, and swollen” (Deut. XXXII). And he added: “He forsook God his maker and departed from God his saviour” (ibid.).

It is therefore clear, O Jews, that you lost your place and nation because you abandoned God, your Creator, in pride of mind. This, then, as has been said, was prefigured by the two servants who remained with the ass: that the Jews were to be separated from one another into two parts, as happened when Solomon sinned. For the house of Israel withdrew from the house of Judah. To them also it is often said through the prophets: [Note: [Col. 0232D] The Lord very often inveighs sharply in the Scriptures against the people for the crime of idolatry, but this remonstrance seems compounded from Jeremiah, chapter III.] “O apostate Israel, O faithless Judah, how grievously you have sinned against God by worshipping [Col. 0232D] idols.”

That ass, O Jews, prefigured your senseless folly. This senseless folly also bore the sacraments of things to come, yet did not know what it bore. But when Abraham said to the young servants, “Wait here with the ass, and after we have worshipped, we shall return to you,” let us introduce the apostle Paul and attend carefully to what he tells us: “Blindness has happened in part to Israel until the fullness of the Gentiles should enter, and thus all Israel should be saved” (Rom. XI). What is “blindness”? Namely, “Wait here with the ass.” “Until the fullness,” he says, “of the Gentiles should enter”—that is, “after we have worshipped,” namely, when the sacrifice of the Lord’s cross has been fulfilled and preached among all nations: this is for the fullness of the Gentiles to enter. And what is “we shall return to you”? Namely, then Israel shall be saved.

The three days in which they came to the place of sacrifice signify the three ages of the world: one before the Law, another under the Law, and the third under grace. Before the Law, from Adam to Moses; under the Law, from Moses to John; from Christ’s birth until now, and whatever remains until the end of the world, is the third day of grace. In that third age, as though after three days, the sacrament of sacrifice was fulfilled. Then Isaac is bound and placed upon the altar, and the Lord, suspended upon the wood, is fastened to the cross. But what was prefigured in Isaac was transferred to the ram. Why? Because Christ is a sheep in respect of simplicity. He is both son and ram: son because born, ram because sacrificed.

But what does it mean that the ram was caught in brambles? For the cross has horns; the two timbers are joined so as to display the form of a cross. Hence it is written of him: “Horns are in his hands” (Hab. III). Therefore the ram caught by its horns prefigured Christ crucified; the brambles, however, are thorns. The thorns signify wicked and sinful people who suspended Jesus Christ, God and man, upon the cross. Thus amid the thorns of your sins, O foolish and malicious Jews, you suspend in the flesh your God and Lord, as he himself complains of you through Jeremiah the prophet: “This people has surrounded me with the thorns of their sins.”

Plainly, then, it has been shown to you, O Jews, how clearly the holy patriarchs before the Law prefigured Christ as to be born of the Virgin, to suffer for humanity’s salvation, to rise on the third day, to ascend into heaven, and on the last day to judge the living and the dead, and, judgment completed, to grant everlasting happiness to his faithful. It is enough, therefore, O Jews, that you have long waited with the ass—that is, remained in the folly of unbelief—and have not arrived with Abraham and Isaac at the place of sacrifice; namely, you have refused until the present day to believe that Jesus Christ, God and man, [Col. 0233D] suffered for the redemption of humankind.

It is therefore necessary that, leaving the ass, you hasten as swiftly as possible to the place of sacrifice: that is, driving from your minds the folly and hardness of your unbelief, you firmly believe that the Son of God and the Virgin suffered for humanity’s salvation; faithfully enter the most holy Church, mother of all the faithful; and receive her sacraments, namely baptism and the other mysteries of Christian religion, with all reverence and devotion. Thus you may attain eternal blessedness with the children of that holy Church, rather than eternal damnation with unbelievers. [Col. 0234A] Therefore do not, by persevering in your malice, become like “the ass and mule, which have no understanding” (Ps. XXXI); for unless you believe Jesus Christ to be true God and true man, sent by God the Father for the redemption of humankind, you can by no means attain the salvation of your souls.

An ass always needs a goad and straw. Therefore, stirred as by a goad by the fear of eternal damnation, drive delay and asinine sluggishness from your hearts. Again, prompted by the desire for eternal reward to receive the true faith, submit yourselves with devout mind to the governance of the Church’s teachers; otherwise, after this life, you will by no means be able to rest in the bosoms of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. For you cannot be saved unless you humbly submit yourselves to their teaching.

§ XIV.—

In the deeds of Jacob and Esau, the rejection of the Jews and the election of Christians will be prefigured. Jacob’s blessing, taken away from the Jews, has been bestowed upon the Christian people through divine grace. The Gentile people, once not God’s people, is now God’s people. Desiring the salvation of souls in a Christian spirit, he adds the useful counsel that they may recover the birthright which they sold for temporal oil, and become sharers in the eternal Father’s blessing of which they have been deprived.

Hold it for certain, O Jews, who have dared to deny that Christ is true God and true man, that I shall grant you no silence and permit you no rest until I have altogether convicted you before God and humankind of being false witnesses by the most true testimonies of the holy Scriptures. [Col. 0234C]

Therefore, to strengthen the catholic faith and expose your utterly false unbelief, I shall willingly bring forward the histories of the ancient Fathers. I urge you diligently to hear how clearly your rejection and the election of Christians were prefigured in the deeds of Jacob and Esau. For thus it is read in the book of Genesis:

“When Isaac was forty years old, he took as wife Rebecca, daughter of Bethuel of Syrian Mesopotamia and sister of Laban. He prayed to the Lord for his wife because she was barren; the Lord heard him and granted Rebecca conception. But the children struggled in her womb, and she said, ‘If this was to happen to me, why was it necessary to conceive?’ Rebecca went to consult the Lord. He answered: ‘Two nations are in your womb, and two peoples shall be divided from your belly. One people shall overcome the other, and the elder shall serve the younger’” (Gen. XXV). [Note: [Col. 0233D] Isidore, *Questions on Genesis*, chap. 23.]

You clearly recognize, O Jews, and need no exposition, how the Church’s people surpasses the Synagogue’s people, and how you, older in time, render service to the younger people of Christians. Indeed, this can also be said allegorically of each of us: for two nations and two peoples are within us, namely those of vices and virtues; but this one is lesser, and that one greater. For the wicked are always more numerous than the good, and vices more numerous than virtues. Yet in us too, by God’s grace, one people overcomes the other, and the greater serves the lesser. For the flesh serves the spirit, and vices yield to virtues.

Esau emerged first from his mother’s womb, red and altogether like a hairy skin. Then his brother Jacob came out, and his hand grasped Esau’s heel. Hence Scripture says: “He held his brother’s sole with his hand.” But why was Esau born wholly red and hairy unless because you, O Jews, first received the Law and were stained by the blood of the innocent and holy prophets, filthy with the stain of sin, foul and shaggy with the squalor of wickedness? Not only did you cruelly shed much righteous blood from righteous Abel to John the Baptist, but you also [Col. 0235B] fastened to the cross without cause the very Redeemer of the world, whose most precious blood you sought to pour upon yourselves and your children not for love but hatred, and not for the forgiveness of sins but for your condemnation.

That the younger brother Jacob held the sole of his elder brother Esau signified that the younger people of Christians, aided by God’s grace, would overcome the older people, namely the Jews, in holiness and righteousness. For Esau’s selling his birthright to his younger brother for food and later being deprived of the paternal blessing owed to him signified that same Israelite people, which, as the book of Exodus states, was called God’s firstborn (Exod. IV). Because of the gains of this present world, it lost not only the honour of its primacy but did not deserve to attain the reward of the heavenly kingdom. The Lord, as it were, reproached and threatened it, saying: “The kingdom of God shall be taken from you and given to a nation”—namely, the Christian people—“bringing forth its fruits” (Matt. XXI).

The birthright itself was the priestly garment, which the eldest, clothed in it with their father’s blessing, wore while offering victims to God as priests. You, O Jews, therefore lost this gift through desire of earthly love, together with the glory of the heavenly kingdom. But now let us hear how Isaac blessed his younger son—that is, the Christian people: “Behold,” he says, “the scent of my son is as the scent of a full field which the Lord has blessed” (Gen. XXVII). The full field has always been the womb of the Virgin Mary. It was then full when it bore within itself the Word, the only-begotten Son of God the Father, clothed in flesh. That womb was truly full because it gave birth to him “in whom all the fullness of divinity dwells bodily” (Col. II).

The fragrance of this fullest field, therefore, is the fame of Christ’s holiness and dignity. Thus the Apostle says: “We are Christ’s good fragrance to God in every place, among those who perish and among those who are saved” (II Cor. II). Hence the bride, that is, the holy Church, says to Jesus Christ, her heavenly bridegroom, in the Song of spiritual love: “We shall run after the fragrance of your ointments” (Cant. I). Let it therefore be said more plainly: “Behold the scent of my son,” namely of the younger son, that is, of the Christian people, “as the scent of a full field”—that is, as the renown or fame of the virtues of Christ’s name, because Christians are named after Christ. The Christian people was thus filled with the fragrance of the full field because the holy Church, spread through the four quarters of the world, was filled with Christ’s faith and spiritual teaching.

I urge you, O Jews, to hear with careful attention, not negligently, how Isaac blessed his younger son—that is, the Christian people, whose figure Jacob bore. “May God give you,” he says, “of the dew of heaven”—that is, the rain of divine words—“and of the fatness of the earth”—that is, abundance from the multitude of faithful peoples; may he also give you abundance of grain and wine”—that is, the most saving communion of the body and blood of that same Redeemer of the world—“and oil” (Gen. XXVII), namely, the anointing of the Holy Spirit. [Col. 0236B]

And he added: “Let peoples serve you”—that is, let those from the Gentiles converted to Christ’s faith by your example be subject to your teaching; “and let tribes worship you”—that is, let those coming from circumcision and receiving ecclesiastical religion reverence you. As you see, O Jews, all these things said are true, because he—that is, the Christian people—is lord of his brothers: Christians rule over you. It follows: “Whoever curses you, let him be cursed; and whoever blesses you, let him be filled with blessings.” You cannot at all deny, O Jews, that this curse has come upon you to this day, because you are convicted of having cursed this younger brother—that is, the Christian people. Therefore you have been cursed by all peoples beneath heaven, because you continually bring cursing against an innocent brother, namely the Christian people.

You have heard, O Jews, your rejection from the history in the book of Genesis, and you have also heard of the election of Christians. Because you always acted contentiously against the Lord and often contradicted his honey-sweet mouth, you lost your birthright and were reckoned a foolish nation. Because you also forgot the Lord your Creator and rendered to alien gods the worship due to him, the paternal blessing was taken from you and bestowed through divine grace upon the Christian people. Thus the blessed apostle Peter says to those very children of the holy Church: “You are a chosen race, a royal priesthood, a holy nation, a people for possession, that you may proclaim the virtues of him who called you from darkness into his marvellous light” (I Pet. II).

Of this people it is said through the prophet Hosea: “Those who were once not a people are now God’s people” (Hos. II). Certainly, the Gentile people, at the time when it served demons, was not God’s people; but now it is truly God’s people because, divine grace going before it, it has devotedly submitted itself to his commands. And it, which once had not obtained mercy, has now obtained mercy from him through God’s grace. It follows: “And it shall be, in the place where it was said, ‘You are not my people,’ there they shall be called children of the living God” (Hos. I).

For, as has been said, the Gentiles did not know the true God and rendered worship not to God but to idols. But after they learned God’s truth, which is Christ, through apostolic preaching, they immediately abandoned the worship of idols and submitted themselves with devout mind to evangelical instruction. Thus the Gentiles, converted to God and strengthened in the catholic faith, were cleansed from sins by holy baptism and received into adoption as children; they who did not deserve to be called the Lord’s people are now, by grace, called children of God.

Hear, therefore, what I say, O Jews; listen to what I speak; attend to what I urge. Behold, you have already lost in the elder brother Esau what you cannot wholly deny: your birthright; and you have forfeited the blessing promised to you. Even unwillingly, you have been made subject to the dominion of the younger brother—that is, of the Christian people [Col. 0237B]. Yet if you yield to my salutary admonitions, if you assent to my counsels, if you are willing to believe me, a Christian man desiring the salvation of your souls, if you give credence to my exhortations, you will be able, together with the younger son—that is, together with the Christian people—to recover the birthright which you formerly sold for temporal pleasures, and to share in the blessing of the eternal Father from which you have been excluded. This, then, is the beneficial counsel for you: that you believe Christ to have been ineffably begotten of God the Father before all ages; to have descended from heaven by the will of the Father for the redemption of the world; to have assumed sinless flesh from the undefiled Virgin; to have suffered, died, [Col. 0237C] and been buried; to have risen on the third day; to have ascended into heaven; now to sit at the right hand of God the Father; and on the last day to be coming thence to judge the living and the dead. This is the Catholic faith: unless you believe it faithfully and steadfastly, you can in no way be saved. But if you keep it firmly, by divine grace cooperating, you will be able to recover the birthright which you sold and the blessing of which you have been deprived, as we have said above. Therefore, if you wish in this present age to cast off the yoke of slavery and in the age to come to rejoice without end with God’s elect, hasten to be baptized by the ministers of the holy Church in the name of the Holy Trinity.

§ XV.—

Jacob’s dream prefigured Christ as begotten of God the Father, as suffering, and as born of the Virgin. [Col. 0237D] The reply of the Jews, who refuse to acknowledge Christ as God, is refuted. The aforesaid patriarch, receiving a sacred name as a vigorous wrestler, prefigures the Lord’s sacrament. On David’s testimony he proves the Jews to be alien and lying children. Joseph, Jacob’s eleventh son, shows forth Christ’s birth, suffering, and resurrection, and likewise the Jews’ faithless obstinacy.

I should like to know, O Jews, whether you now believe, having laid aside the hardness of unbelief, that Jesus Christ is true God and true man, or whether you still [Col. 0238A] doubt something concerning him. I do not wish you to hide yourselves beneath a silence of malice and wickedness; rather, set forth openly what you think of him. This is your answer. You say that it seems unbelievable to you that the Son of God descended from the bosom of the Father, assumed human nature, and suffered and died. Since, therefore, you say that a scruple of doubt still remains in your minds, listen attentively, O Jews, enemies of truth, while I explain how the patriarch Jacob, in his deeds, prefigured the Son of God himself as begotten of God the Father before all ages, and as born of the Virgin and suffering for the redemption of the world. [Note: [Col. 0237D] Isidore, ibid., ch. 24.]

Jacob, then, proceeding into Mesopotamia came to a place called Bethel. He put a stone beneath his head, and, while asleep, saw in a dream [Col. 0238B] a ladder standing upon the earth, whose top touched heaven; moreover, angels of God were ascending and descending by it. When he saw this, he awoke and anointed the stone, saying: “Truly this is the house of God and the gate of heaven” (Gen. 28). This dream of Jacob signified Christ’s passion, or death. The stone placed under his head and afterwards anointed signified Christ, the Anointed One. For who does not know that Christ is so called from anointing?

[Note: [Col. 0237D] The following words are absent here: “But the house of God, because Christ was born there in Bethlehem.” Yet Blessed Martin very rightly omitted them, inserting from another passage of Isidore why Bethel is interpreted “house of God,” [Col. 0238D] whereas Bethlehem is called “house of bread” because of that bread which descended there from heaven, as Isidore himself says in that chapter of the *Etymologies*.]

It should be noted, as Blessed Isidore, our patron, says in the book of the *Etymologies*, that the Jebusites founded Bethel, a city of Samaria, which was formerly called Luz. But after Jacob, sleeping there, saw the ladder leaning upon heaven and said, “Truly this is the house [Col. 0238C] of God and the gate of heaven,” the place received from this circumstance the name Bethel, that is, “house of God.” But when golden calves were made there by Jeroboam, it was called Betheun [Note: [Col. 0238D] Isidore: Bethaven.], that is, “house of an idol,” though it had formerly been called “house of God.” It is called the gate of heaven because the Son of God descended from heaven into that land and from there again ascended to heaven.

Alternatively, the house of God is called the gate of heaven because the prayers and vows offered there by the faithful ascend even to the throne of divine mercy; and there God mercifully ascends to those who humbly entreat him. Further, the ladder is Christ, who said: “I am the way”; and again: “No one comes to the Father except through me” (John 14). Through this Son of God and of the Virgin, therefore, the angels ascended and descended; by these angels are signified [Col. 0238D] the evangelists and all Christ’s preachers. They ascend when, in order to understand his most surpassing divinity, they rise above every creature, so as to find him in the beginning, true God with God, through whom all things were made (John 1). They descend to him when they find him “made of a woman, made under the law, that he might redeem those who were under the law” (Gal. 4). For that ladder reached from earth to heaven—that is, from flesh to spirit—because upon it, [Col. 0239A] that is, in Christ, the carnal become spiritual by advancing, as though ascending. The spiritual themselves descend to those whom they nourish, still more simply, with milk, when in some manner they cannot speak to them as to spiritual persons but as to carnal persons.

Thus Jesus Christ, God and man, is above in his head—that is, in God the Father—and below in his body, which is the Church. Therefore one ascends to this Son of God and of the Virgin in order that he may be understood in the heights; one descends to him again so that he may be nourished as a little one in his members. Through him the faithful are raised up, that they may contemplate him exaltedly at the right hand of God the Father; through him they humble themselves, that they may obediently proclaim him who is exalted. It has therefore been shown to you sufficiently clearly, O Jews, that Jesus [Col. 0239B] Christ, God and man, was foreshadowed from the beginning of the world in the figures and enigmas of the patriarchs; was announced beforehand by the voices of the prophets; and was openly displayed by the proclamations of apostles and evangelists—so fully that no doubt concerning him ought now to remain in your hearts.

Therefore, constrained by charity, O Jews, I counsel you to ascend faithfully by this ladder, that is, through Jesus Christ, so that you may believe him to be one true God with God the Father and the Holy Spirit. Also descend through him humbly and faithfully, so that you do not doubt that he assumed human flesh without sin from his virgin Mother. If through him you ascend to the Son coeternal with God the Father, you will find him begotten of God the Father before all ages [Col. 0239C]; if through him you descend, you will plainly know that for the redemption of the world he suffered, died, and was buried, and rose from the tomb on the third day. Therefore ascend in steadfast belief to him, true God and true man, so that through him you may ascend to the joys of eternal life.

Therefore reveal openly to us the inclination or purpose of your hearts, O Jews, so that, if you now believe Jesus Christ to be true God, having put aside the treachery of unbelief, we may give thanks to the same God and man, Jesus Christ, for your illumination. But if not, we shall bring forward further and further testimonies from the Old and New Testaments in order to convict your unbelief and strengthen our faith. [Col. 0239D] In reply you object that you do not wish to receive as God one whom your fathers were once able to accuse before a judge, nail to the cross, and, according to their will, hand over to a most shameful death. To this we answer you: the greater the injury you say that they inflicted upon him, the more you are bound to believe faithfully in him and to show him greater reverence. The greater the contempt he endured from you, as you say, the more you are bound to obey him. Nor, as you falsely allege, were your forebears able to nail him to the cross; rather, he himself of his own free will chose to mount the cross for the redemption of the world. [Col. 0240A] Therefore, do not be scandalized because the Son of God and of the Virgin chose to suffer for the salvation of humankind, since the patriarch Jacob long before prefigured in his deeds both that same voluntary passion and your, so to speak, adamantine unbelief.

And so that you may not doubt that this is as I have said, I urge you to hear prudently the history of that time. [Note: [Col. 0239D] Isidore, *Questions on Genesis*, ch. 27.] For twenty years Jacob served Laban, the brother of his mother Rebecca. Returning from there, he came to a torrent; after everything belonging to him had been brought across the torrent, he himself remained alone. And behold, a man wrestled with him until morning. Jacob prevailed and did not let him go until he obtained a blessing from him and received the sacred name Israel [Col. 0240B] (Gen. 32), in which the image of the Lord’s sacrament was principally prefigured.

Attend carefully, O Jews, to what is said, lest—God forbid!—you depart empty from this sacred reading. That man, then, most evidently bore the type of Christ; yet Jacob prevailed over him only because he was willing, so that he might prefigure the mystery of the Lord’s passion. There Jacob was seen, in the type of the Jews—that is, in the offspring of his own body—to prevail over the incarnate Son of God, and, as though against one weak and feeble, to enter into contest with his flesh and prevail in his passion. For the Jews seemed to prevail against the humanity of the Son of God in the passion when they cried aloud to Pilate, saying: “Take him away, take him away; crucify him, for if [Col. 0240C] you release this man, you are not Caesar’s friend” (John 19). “And their voices prevailed” (Luke 23). Yet Jacob obtained a blessing from the same angel whom he had overcome as victor; the imposition of that name was indeed a blessing. Israel is interpreted “a man seeing God,” which will be the reward of the saints at the end.

Yet the angel touched the breadth of his thigh and made him lame. But what did it signify, O Jews, that Jacob was one and the same man, both blessed and lame? It signified, plainly, that he was blessed in those of his offspring who believed in Christ, and lame in those who to this day stubbornly deny him. For the sinew, or breadth, of the thigh is the multitude of a people. Indeed, there are more in his stock [Col. 0240D] who, having fallen away from the faith of their father, namely Jacob himself, and having departed from the command of their Creator, limp along the paths of their error.

Truly, O Jews, you have fallen away from the faith of the patriarchs: the faith of the Holy Trinity which they firmly held in their hearts through belief and love, and prefigured in their works, you cast away beneath the foot of pride. You also unhappily depart from the command of your Creator and limp along the paths of your manifold error, while [lacuna: you deny, or are unwilling to believe in] Jesus Christ, God and man, [Note: [Col. 0239] Supply “you deny,” or “you are unwilling to believe,” or something similar, to complete the sense of the sentence.] whom God the Father prefigured through the patriarchs as one who would come for the redemption of the world, foretold through the prophets, and plainly showed through the apostles and evangelists to have now come and [Col. 0241A] conversed with humankind (Baruch 3).

Concerning this certainly condemnable unbelief of your minds, Jesus Christ himself, God and man, complains of you, O Jews, through the Psalmist, saying: “Alien children have lied to me; alien children have grown old, and have limped from their paths” (Ps. 17). Therefore the Lord Jesus Christ calls you, O senseless Jews, not children of Abraham but alien children, because you have fallen away from the faith and righteousness of Abraham the patriarch. Rightly he says that you are not his but alien children, because, although he had been sent by God the Father to deliver you and the entire world, you did not reverently receive him as truly God and the Son of God, nor receive his preaching with devout minds; rather, during his passion you shook your heads against him [Col. 0241B] and cried out mockingly: “Ha! You who destroy the temple of God and rebuild it in three days, save yourself by coming down from the cross” (Matt. 27; Mark 15).

Hence he also speaks, as though making a complaint, through the prophet Isaiah: “I have nourished and exalted children, but they, despising me, have rejected me. The ox knows its owner, and the ass its master’s manger; Israel has not known me, my people has not understood me” (Isa. 1). Since, therefore, you are not children of God but alien children—that is, children of the devil—you have lied to Jesus Christ, God and man, and have become far estranged from him. In what have you lied? Namely, in saying that he was not the Son of God but the son of Joseph the carpenter (Matt. 13). Elsewhere too [Col. 0241C] you were found false witnesses in lying against him: when Pilate wished to release him, saying, “I find no cause of death in him” (John 18), you cried out insistently with loud voices: “If this man were not an evildoer, we would not have handed him over to you” (Matt. 28). Elsewhere also you lied, O Jews, when you gave abundant money to the governor’s guards and instructed them to say that his disciples came by night and stole his body by night while you were asleep.

“Alien children,” he says, “have lied to me; alien children have grown old,” and so forth. It is as though Jesus Christ, God and man, said to you more plainly: “Children who chose rather to estrange themselves from me by worshipping idols and committing countless crimes against my laws, than to remain with me in humble obedience, [Col. 0241D] have grown old.” As though he said: “They chose rather to remain in the oldness of the first man than to walk with me in newness of life.” “And they have limped from their paths.” It is as though the Son of God and of the Virgin said openly: “Because the Jews withdrew from me by living wickedly, they limped from their paths; that is, they have been made lame by their own evil inventions, possessing neither the right foot—that is, spiritual understanding in the Law—nor Christ in the faith of the Holy Trinity.”

Truly, O Jews, because you do not believe that Christ has already come and was true God and true man, you not only limp with the right foot, but you also grow sluggish in good works pleasing to God, so that you can no longer beget spiritual [Col. 0242A] children. Finally, Jacob the patriarch’s additional statement that he had seen God face to face, though he had related above that a man wrestled with him, signified that the same person would be God and man, who would wrestle in his passion with the Israelite people.

It has also been shown openly to you, O Jews, how clearly the blessing or freedom of Christians and your unbelief were prefigured in the patriarch Jacob. How long, therefore, O Jews, will you limp from your paths—that is, from your unlawful inventions—and refuse to walk with upright steps of faith? Why do you disdain to walk in the way of righteousness, and proceed, limping in foot, through the rough and craggy places of folly? You limp, indeed, with the foot of unbelief, since you refuse with proud minds to give faith to the most truthful testimonies of the sacred Law, the words of the prophets, [Col. 0242B] and the most lucid testimonies of the holy evangelists, all declaring that he is true God and true man. Since you do not hold the Catholic faith, you have no right foot; since you trust in your false assertions, you limp with the left.

Truly, O unhappy Jews, in limping you hasten toward eternal damnation, since, by denying, blaspheming, and bringing false testimony against Christ—the most straight way—you abandon him. Nor do you beget, by holy admonitions, children belonging to the heavenly Jerusalem; instead, by false persuasions, you cast them with yourselves into Gehenna. Since, therefore, as has been said, you have no right foot in upright conduct, [Col. 0242C] nor spiritual understanding in the divine Scriptures, nor believe in your hearts that Jesus Christ is one true God with God the Father and the Holy Spirit, you hasten, certainly, not to life but to eternal destruction without any intervening delay.

This hatred arising from your unbelief, and the enmity which you unjustly bear toward the Son of God, were undoubtedly prefigured by Jacob’s eleven sons, who, envying their brother Joseph, stripped him of his tunic and sold him to the Ishmaelites. Therefore, to refute your false faithlessness and to strengthen our faith more and more, let us recall the history of that time and all listen attentively together to its spiritual exposition.

[Note: [Col. 0241D] Isidore, *Questions on Genesis*, ch. 30.] Joseph, then, one of Jacob’s twelve sons, [Col. 0242D] whom his father loved above all his sons, prefigured the Lord Jesus Christ, whom God the Father preferred above the other brothers descended from Abraham’s line, as one born according to the flesh from the Virgin. Hence it is also said there that Jacob begot him in old age. For as the world grew old, the rising Son of God came late through the childbirth of the most blessed Virgin Mary, as though a son of old age according to the mystery of the body he assumed, because he was with the Father before all ages. The many-coloured tunic which the father made for him signified the diversity of peoples from all nations gathered together in Christ’s body.

That dream in which the sheaves of his brothers worshipped his sheaf is what was fulfilled in Christ: “All kings of the earth shall worship him,” says the Psalmist; “all nations shall serve him” (Ps. 71), namely by offering the fruit of good works. For he is the one whom the sun, moon, and stars worship. Of him it is written: “Praise him, sun and moon; and all stars and light” (Ps. 148). The excellence of the saints, under the name of the sun, and the multitude of all peoples in the figure of the stars, under the image of the Church’s charity, worship him. Therefore Jacob rebukes his son Joseph, saying: “Shall I, and your mother, and your brothers worship you upon the earth?” (Gen. 37). This rebuke of the father signified the pride of your unbelief, O Jews: because you know Christ to have been born of Jacob’s seed, [Col. 0243B] you disdain to worship him. What ought to make you love him more, receive him with the greatest devotion, and believe faithfully in him, is precisely what makes you despise him more and obstinately resist his most truthful preaching.

Hence he himself says: “A prophet is not without honour except in his own country, and in his own house, and among his own kin” (Mark 6). I want you to know, O Jews, that Jesus Christ, God and man, called himself a prophet because, in order to strengthen the souls of his faithful in the right faith, he revealed the past to them, showed them the present, and foretold the future. For Moses the lawgiver bore true witness to you concerning him, saying: “God will raise up for you a prophet from among your brethren like me; him [Col. 0243C] you shall hear in all things whatsoever he shall speak to you” (Deut. 18). To show also how great was the power and dignity of this Son of God and of the Virgin, he added: “Every person who does not hear that prophet shall be cut off from his people” (ibid.). The prophet Isaiah also says of him: “Behold, a great prophet shall come, and he himself shall renew Jerusalem.”

This great prophet, therefore, came forth from God the Father and received our humanity from his virgin Mother. Yet you, O Jews, did not receive him with reverence and honour; rather, like shameless dogs, you often assailed him with reproaches and insults. Therefore, when, filled with a diabolical spirit, you said to him with polluted mouths, “You have a demon,” he rebuked you with complete justice and moderation: “I do not have a demon, but I honour my Father, and you have dishonoured [Col. 0243D] me” (John 8). And again: “I came in the name of my Father, and you did not receive me; but if another comes in his own name, you will receive him” (John 5)—namely Antichrist, whom you, O Jews, await, and with whom I greatly fear that you will perish eternally.

The aforementioned saying is therefore true: “A prophet is not without honour except in his own country” (Mark 6), because Jesus Christ, God and man, was received with the highest honour and reverence by other nations, but by you was mocked, despised, and assailed with insults and countless injuries.

This obstinacy of your unbelief, therefore, as we said above, O Jews, was prefigured by the patriarch Jacob when he rebuked his son Joseph and said: “Shall I, and your mother, and your brothers worship you [Col. 0244A] upon the earth?” (Gen. 37). It is as though the patriarch Jacob said more plainly to Jesus Christ, Son of God and of the Virgin, whom he prefigured in these words: “Shall I, namely Israel, from whose seed you are to be born according to the flesh, and your mother, the Synagogue, and your brothers, namely all the Jews, worship you upon the earth?” The reason is therefore plain, O Jews, why you disdain to worship him: you know that he was born from Abraham’s offspring. But now let us hear what follows.

Jacob sent his son Joseph to take thought for his brothers, and God the Father sent his only-begotten Son to visit the human race weakened by sins. He is sent by that Father of whom it is written: “God sent his Son in the likeness of sinful flesh” (Rom. 8), that he might visit the sheep wandering without the true shepherd and call them back to ever-green pastures. Therefore he himself, the most merciful shepherd, says: “I am the good shepherd; and I know my own, and my own know me” (John 10). Of these sheep Blessed Peter says in the Catholic Epistle: “You were formerly like wandering sheep, but now you have been converted to the shepherd and bishop of your souls” (1 Pet. 2).

Joseph found his brothers in Dothaim, which is interpreted “defection.” Truly they were in a great defection, since they were planning to kill their brother. When they saw him from afar, before he came near them, they planned to kill him. And when the Jews saw the true Joseph, that is, the Lord [Col. 0244C] Jesus Christ, they all formed one plan to crucify him, saying to Pilate: “Crucify, crucify him” (John 19). For Joseph’s brothers said: “A most evil beast has devoured him” (Gen. 37). The Jews too were a most evil beast, for they handed Christ over to death, though they found no falsehood in his mouth and had never seen him sin. Truly the Jewish people itself was a most evil beast, concerning whom Jesus Christ himself, God and man, said: “Many dogs have surrounded me; the council of evildoers has besieged me” (Ps. 21). And again: “Many calves have surrounded me; fat bulls have besieged me” (ibid.). Of them Jesus Christ, God and man, also said to his disciples: “Behold, I send you as sheep among wolves” (Matt. 10).

[Col. 0244D] Let it therefore be said: “A most evil beast devoured Joseph”—that is, the bloody beast, the Jewish people, killed Christ. Joseph’s brothers stripped him of his long and many-coloured tunic; after the death of the cross, the Jews stripped the Lord Jesus Christ of the bodily many-coloured tunic—that is, the tunic adorned by the diversity of every virtue. They sprinkled Joseph’s tunic with a goat’s blood; and the Jews accused Christ with false charges and testimonies. Then Joseph is cast into a cistern, and Christ, stripped of human flesh, descended into hell to free his own who were held there. Joseph is also lifted out of the cistern and sold to the Ishmaelites—that is, the Gentiles—and Christ, after returning from the lower regions, is bought by all nations through the commerce of faith. The former is sold for a price at [Col. 0245A] Judah’s counsel, and Christ is sold for thirty pieces of silver by the counsel of Judas Iscariot.

Then Jacob, grieving the losses of his descendants, mourned as a father for his lost son and, as a prophet, O unhappy Jews, mourned your destruction. For he foresaw that by sinning you would depart from the Lord, lose the inheritance promised to you by him, and be handed over into captivity to all the nations under heaven. Finally, Jacob tore his garment, which we read that the chief priest did at the passion of the Son of God and of the Virgin. That holy patriarch tore his garment to show that his people would be stripped of heavenly gifts, that the Israelite kingdom would be divided into two parts, and that it would be laid waste within itself. Foreseeing this, the Lord said: “Every kingdom divided against itself shall be laid waste, and house shall fall upon house” (Luke 11). The veil of the Temple, torn at Christ’s passion, signified this as well.

Therefore, O Jews, from the beginning of the world the holy patriarchs, as has been said, showed beforehand in figures and enigmas that this same Jesus Christ would come for the redemption of the world. The truthful prophets, taught by the Holy Spirit, foretold in the truest proclamations that he was begotten of God the Father before all ages and would be born, true God and true man, from his virgin Mother without a man’s embrace. The holy apostles plainly showed in the clearest words that he was conceived of the Holy Spirit, born of his virgin Mother, [Col. 0245C] and has already redeemed the human race by his passion and cross. The teachers of the Old and New Testaments maintain that he is true God and true man, and prove you—who deny him with proud minds and obstinate hearts—to be wholly false witnesses. Armed with the most truthful arguments of the Law and the prophets, they nullify your false assertion and demonstrate in every way that you have lied.

Therefore, O Jews, believe without doubt that the Son of God assumed real flesh from Jacob’s line; worship with us him who reigns at the right hand of God the Father. Embrace with the arms of true faith and piety him whom you purchased for thirty pieces of silver and nailed to the cross without cause, so that through him [Col. 0245D] you may attain the joys of eternal blessedness. Believe that he whose name you wished maliciously to erase from beneath heaven reigns everywhere with God the Father and the Holy Spirit, so that you may obtain pardon for the past hardness of your unbelief.

The sun worships him—that is, the excellence of the angels, archangels, and all the heavenly orders of blessed spirits, who have remained in love for Jesus Christ, the same God and man through whom God the Father created all things. The moon also worships him—that is, the holy Church, of which Solomon, marvelling in the Song of spiritual love, says among other things: “Who is this that comes up like the rising dawn, fair as the moon, chosen as the sun, terrible as an army drawn up in battle array?” (Song 6). For the holy Church advances as a rising [Col. 0246A] dawn, because, having left the darkness of sins behind, it is renewed in the knowledge and love of its Redeemer. The stars also worship him: namely, all the saints shining with the brightness of diverse virtues.

What do you say to these things, O Jews? What answer or objection do you make? Do you still not give faith to truth so manifest, which is Christ? Do you still not assent to receive the true faith, although the most truthful testimonies of the Law and prophets, agreeing most truly among themselves that Christ is true God and true man, are set before you? Meanwhile, I should like to know, O Jews, whether the treachery of your unbelief has now been wholly expelled from your hearts and whether you wish to receive the Catholic faith with the greatest devotion, or whether you still intend to remain in your malice.

§ XVI.—

The prophecy of the patriarch Jacob plainly demonstrates that, in the succession of Judah’s kingdom, the ruler has failed, and that Christ has already come and suffered. By the patriarch’s prophetic spirit the teachers of the Church and the holy Gospels are commended. The patriarch’s blessing of Ephraim and Manasseh, together with the mystery of the cross, plainly prefigures the election of the Church’s religion and the rejection of Jewish observance. The aforesaid patriarch foresaw the deadly obstinacy of Jewish perversity in the sons Simeon and Levi, whose indignation was harsh and accursed.

If, therefore, any scruple concerning Christ’s coming or divinity remains in your minds, make this known to us, so that we may know of what faith or what [Col. 0246C] disposition you are. To this you reply, O Jews, that you do not believe Christ has already come, but still await his coming. Thus you say that he has not yet come, but testify that he will come at the end of the world. O perverse and faithless race! O nation without salutary counsel and without spiritual prudence! With so many testimonies of the Law agreeing that Christ is true God; with so many prophecies agreeing that he truly assumed our humanity; with so many most truthful proclamations of the evangelists affirming the same—that by his cross and passion he has already beyond doubt rescued the world from the devil’s power, risen from death, ascended into heaven, and now sits glorified at the right hand of God the Father who sent him—do you still, after dismissing every doubt, fail wholly to believe?

O foolish and senseless people! Do you not know that the one you await as coming at the end of the world will not be the Son of God but a vessel full of the devil? Do you not know, O blind nation, that the one whom you say will come will not be the most merciful saviour of souls but a most cruel deceiver? Know certainly and do not doubt at all that he in whom you place your hope will not come to redeem the human race, but to bring it with himself to eternal damnation. Nor will he be a minister of righteousness or peace, but of discord and every kind of wickedness.

Therefore, O unhappy—indeed, most unhappy—Jews: because you obstinately deny that the Son of God and of the Virgin, who was born under King Herod and suffered under Pontius Pilate for the redemption of the world, has already come, [Col. 0247A] and because you place the hope of your salvation in Antichrist, who will certainly be rebellious and contrary to God in his evil works, so that you may perish with him, let the patriarch Jacob, whom you can neither wholly contradict nor ought to contradict, come forward and, in your hearing, bear witness whether he has already come or is still to come.

Speak, holy Jacob; speak concerning Christ’s coming what you learned by the revelation of the Holy Spirit, so that by your most truthful testimony the faithlessness of the Jews may be convicted and the Catholic faith strengthened ever more fully in every respect. Speak, then, of Christ what you know, so that faithless Jews, convicted by your most certain authority, may quickly cast from their hearts the folly of deadly unbelief and, removing all doubt, faithfully believe with us that Christ has already come and was true God and true man.

“The sceptre,” he says, “shall not be taken away from Judah, nor a ruler from his thigh, until he comes who is to be sent; and he shall be the expectation of the Gentiles” (Gen. 49). It is evident, O Jews, and you cannot deny it, that the sceptre was not taken from Judah—that is, the power of governing the Jewish people—nor did a ruler fail from his thigh, until he came who was to be sent by God the Father for the redemption of the world, namely Christ. And he was the expectation of the Gentiles because at his coming he benefited not Jews only but Gentiles also. Some Gentiles indeed awaited Christ’s coming and the redemption of the world: Job, Balaam, Nebuchadnezzar—to whom the mystery [Col. 0247C] of his incarnation was revealed—the Sibyl, Virgil, and many others whom we cannot adequately enumerate.

Therefore, O Jews, an unbroken royal succession from Judah’s seed remained among you until Christ was sent by God the Father through the Virgin for the redemption of the world. The histories of your books prove this, O Jews, enemies of truth: they plainly show that Herod was the first foreign-born king among your people, under whom the Son of God and of the Virgin was born according to the flesh. Therefore, O Jews who maintain that Christ has not yet come, show us a royal sceptre—that is, a man descended from Judah’s progeny who possesses royal power among you. If, as you falsely claim, Christ has not yet come, why did a ruler from Judah’s thigh fail long ago? You who assert that Christ has not come but is still to come must therefore show a ruler of the Israelite people from Judah’s lineage. But if, as is true, you cannot show a prince from Judah’s progeny, you must believe with us beyond doubt that Christ has already come.

This aforesaid prophecy of the patriarch Jacob, therefore, O Jews, plainly demonstrates that the ruler from the tribe of Judah has failed and that Christ has already come; it manifestly proves you false witnesses in your assertion. Therefore, beyond doubt, the ruler has now failed from Judah’s thigh, because he who was to be sent by God the Father for the redemption of the world has already come.

[Col. 0248A] Hear also, O Jews, what the patriarch Jacob goes on to say, in order to strengthen the catholic faith and overcome your most mendacious unbelief, concerning this same Jesus Christ, Son of God and of the Virgin, who was to be born according to the flesh from the tribe of Judah: “He shall bind his colt to the vine” (Gen. XLIX). [Note: [Col. 0247] From Isidore, as are most of the other passages, *Questions on Genesis*, ch. 31.] Christ’s colt is the people of the Gentiles, upon whom the burden of the Law had never yet been imposed. At his coming Christ bound this colt—that is, the Gentile people—to the vine: he joined them by faith to the apostles, prophets, patriarchs, and other saints from among the Jews who believed in him. For “the vineyard of the Lord of hosts is the house of Israel.” It follows: “And he shall bind his ass to the vine.” For he himself says of himself: “I am the true vine” (John XV). To this vine [Col. 0248B] the Son of God and of the Virgin bound his ass, upon which he sat; that is, he joined to himself his Church gathered from Jews and Gentiles. Thus God-and-man Jesus Christ bound her to the vine of his body by the bond [Note: [Col. 0247D] “By a bond.”] of charity and the connection of evangelical discipline, so that, living in imitation of him, she might become an heir of God and a co-heir with Christ (Rom. VIII).

Again the patriarch Jacob adds: “He shall wash his robe in wine, and his cloak in the blood of grapes.” It is as though he said: He who is to be sent by God the Father, namely Jesus Christ, shall wash his robe—that is, his flesh—in the blood of his passion; or, he shall wash his Church in that wine “which shall be shed for many for the remission of sins” (Matt. [Col. 0248C] XXVI). “And his cloak in the blood of grapes.” The cloak is the Gentiles, whom Christ joined to his body, as it is written: “As I live, says the Lord, unless I clothe myself with men as with a garment” (Isa. XLIX). Isaiah likewise says to her: “With all these you shall clothe yourself as with an ornament” (ibid.). Christ cleansed these—namely, Jews and Gentiles who faithfully believed in him—from their sins in his blood when he hung like a cluster of grapes on the wood of the cross. Then blood and water flowed from his side; the water of baptism washed us from our sins, while by the blood he redeemed us from the hand of the ancient enemy.

Hear, O Jews, what I say; hear what I speak. While the patriarch Jacob, blessing his son Judah, says that Jesus Christ, who was to be born from the tribe of Judah, [Col. 0248D] would wash his robe—that is, the holy Church—in the blood of his passion, he most plainly contradicts you false witnesses, who deny that he has already come and suffered for the redemption of the world. For we do not read that Judah suffered or washed his robe in wine; rather, we believe that this was spiritually foretold concerning Christ. Let us hear also what he adds: “His eyes are more beautiful than wine, and his teeth whiter than milk.” The eyes of Jesus Christ are the apostles and evangelists, who supply the light of knowledge to the whole body of the Church. They are shown to be more beautiful than wine because their teaching surpasses the astringency of old wine—that is, the traditions of the ancient Law. For evangelical [Col. 0249A] precepts are far clearer than the commandments of the Old Testament. “And his teeth,” he says, “are whiter than milk.” The teeth are the holy preachers, who cut people away from errors and transfer them, as though by eating them, into Christ’s body. By “milk” is signified the teaching of the Law, which nourished the carnal people, like a little child, with a cup of milk. Christ’s teeth—that is, the teachers of the Church—have become whiter than this, because they chew and distribute the strong, substantial food of the word. Of them the Apostle says in the Epistle to the Hebrews: “Solid food is for the perfect” (Heb. V). Jacob the patriarch rightly called Christ’s teeth whiter than milk. For all who are perfect, and who, expounding the food of Scripture, provide the Church’s body with the subtle understanding called [Col. 0249B] spiritual, ought to be white, pure, and free from every stain.

You ought to understand, O Jews, that, as Jacob says, the eyes of Jesus Christ—that is, the apostles, evangelists, and other teachers of the Church—are more beautiful than wine: their teaching is clearer, sweeter, and subtler than the carnal observances of the Mosaic Law (Exod. XXI). There an eye was commanded to be taken for an eye; but the Church’s teachers command people to forgive one another and not return evil for evil. Therefore, since through the mouth of so great a patriarch, filled with the prophetic Spirit, O Jews, the eyes of Jesus Christ—that is, the teachers of the Church—are praised, and their evangelical [Col. 0249C] and spiritual [Note: [Col. 0249D] “Spiritual.”] teaching is preferred to the ordinances of the ancient Law, you must submit yourselves with devout minds to their governance and salutary counsel, and receive through their ministry the sacraments of the Church’s religion; otherwise you will never be able to attain eternal joys. I do not wish you to be ignorant, O Jews, that whether one is Jew or Gentile, unless he receives Christ’s baptism through the ministers of the holy Church, he cannot be saved at all. Therefore be assured that, unless you receive the catholic faith and are baptized in the name of the holy Trinity—namely, Father, Son, and Holy Spirit—you will by no means be able to rest in Abraham’s bosom after this life. For all of you who descend from Abraham’s stock will be able to attain the salvation of [Col. 0249D] your souls only through Christ. You must therefore abandon the carnal observances of the Law if you are to attain eternal joys. Jacob the patriarch indeed prefigured this future election of the Church’s religion and rejection of Jewish observance when he blessed Joseph’s two sons. Therefore, O Jews, that you may plainly know that what we say is true, I urge you to listen attentively to the history of that time as expounded spiritually.

[Note: [Col. 0249D] Isidore, ibid.] Joseph, hastening to receive his father Jacob’s blessing, presented his two sons to him, Manasseh and Ephraim. But the elder, Manasseh, whose name means “forgetfulness,” bore the type of the Jewish people, [Col. 0250A] who forgot the Lord their God who made them. To them Moses the lawgiver, full of the spirit of prophecy, said: “You abandoned the God who begot you, and forgot the Lord your Creator” (Deut. XXXII). Ephraim, however, the younger, whose name signifies “fruitfulness,” bore the type of the Christian people, made fruitful throughout the breadth of the world. When Jacob wished to bless them, Joseph placed Ephraim at his left hand and set Manasseh at the grandfather’s right. But Jacob, crossing his hands and prefiguring the mystery of the cross, transferred his right hand to the younger and placed his left over the elder. Thus the likeness of the cross, marked over their heads, signified a stumbling-block for the Jews but future glory for Christians (I Cor. I). Therefore, through the mystery of the cross, we see the elder made left-handed from right-handed, and [Col. 0250B] the younger right-handed from left-handed: for, as the Jews fall away on our left, we have obtained their glory. By such a sacrament the lesser people of the Gentiles was set above the greater people of the Jews. Of them the same patriarch says: “This one indeed,” namely Manasseh, “shall become a people; but that one,” namely Ephraim, “shall be exalted” (Gen. XLVIII).

You have heard, O Jews, how plainly, in the figures of the patriarchs, the testimonies of the Law, and the proclamations of the prophets, by God’s disposing grace, the liberty of Christians and your servitude were prefigured from the beginning of the world. For because you arrogantly cast Christ’s Gospel and his disciples out of your borders, you justly lost the land of promise and were delivered into servitude to the same [Col. 0250C] Christian people. You, together with your rulers and priests, crucified without cause God-and-man Jesus Christ, who had delivered you from Egyptian bondage and had come again to call you into the liberty of God’s children. Together with those same murderous rulers and priests, you were expelled with great disgrace from the inheritance promised to you and for some time possessed by your fathers. Thus it happened to you as the Son of God and of the Virgin himself foretold: “Your house shall be left to you desolate” (Matt. XXIII). By a just judgment, therefore, you were driven from the land of promise; and, as unbelievers defiled by the blood of the world’s Redeemer, you were scattered throughout the world and handed over in servitude to all nations under heaven.

[Col. 0250D] Without doubt the patriarch Jacob, full of the spirit of prophecy, foresaw the deadly obstinacy of your unbelief as something future in the race descended from him; and he spoke with a kind of indignation to his sons Simeon and Levi: “Simeon and Levi, vessels of iniquity, waging war. Let not my soul enter into their counsel, nor my glory be in their assembly; for in their fury they killed a man, and in their will they undermined a wall. Cursed be their fury, for it is obstinate; and their indignation, for it is harsh. I will divide them in Jacob and scatter them in Israel” (Gen. XLIX). [Note: [Col. 0250D] Isidore, ibid.] I urge you, O Jews, not to pass carelessly over the true history of so great a patriarch, [Col. 0251A] but to listen attentively to its exposition. “Simeon,” he says, “and Levi, vessels of iniquity, waging war.” By Simeon and Levi are understood the scribes and priests of the Jewish people. From Simeon come the scribes of the Jews; from the tribe of Levi, the chief priests. Of them the Evangelist says: “The chief priests took counsel to kill Jesus” (Matt. XXVI). Concerning this council the holy patriarch, who already foresaw in the Spirit that Christ would suffer for the salvation of the human race, says: “Let not my soul enter into their counsel.” This holy patriarch shuddered even then to see such crimes as the Jews would commit in the last times. It follows: “For in their fury they killed a man,” namely Jesus Christ. This was also foretold in the book [Note: [Col. 0251] More correctly than Isidore: Isaiah; although the author, like the holy Father, cites this passage more fully and somewhat differently.] of Wisdom in the person of the Jews: “Come, let us beset the righteous man, because he is useless to us and opposed to our deeds. Let us condemn him to a most shameful death, for there will be a reckoning according to his words” (Wis. II). Again Jacob adds: “In their will they undermined a wall.” It is as though he said more plainly: In their perverse will they wounded with a lance that spiritual and most strong bulwark which guards Israel, namely the Saviour’s side. It follows: “Cursed be their fury, for it is obstinate,” namely in committing so great a crime. Truly the fury of the Jews was cursed and obstinate, because, inflamed by the anger of diabolical cruelty, they presented Christ to Pontius [Col. 0251C] Pilate the governor, saying: “Crucify, crucify him; for if you release this man, you are not Caesar’s friend” (John XIX). Their indignation also proved cursed and harsh when they demanded the robber Barabbas and appointed Christ, the author of life, to be crucified. Again he adds, saying: “I will divide them in Jacob and scatter them in Israel.” Therefore these two, Simeon and Levi, are called division and scattering: because some among them believed in the Lord, while others remained in unbelief. Those who are separated from unbelieving Jews and faithfully joined to the children of the Church are called divided; those whose country and Temple having been destroyed, their unbelieving race is scattered throughout the world, are called scattered.

Therefore it is necessary, O Jews, for your admonition, that we repeat what the patriarch Jacob, full of the spirit [Col. 0251D] of prophecy, foretold above concerning the unbelief of you and your fathers: “Cursed,” he says, “be their fury, for it is obstinate; and their indignation, for it is harsh.” Truly the fury of your fathers was cursed, because they stubbornly delivered Jesus Christ into the hands of the Gentiles to be crucified. Their fury was obstinate and cursed because it fastened the Son of God and of the Virgin to the cross without cause, hurled them into the depths of hell, unhappily expelled you from the land of promise, and subjected you to the servitude of all nations. Your fathers themselves, when by an unjust judgment they condemned God-and-man Jesus [Col. 0252A] Christ as guilty of death, were cursed because they delivered themselves to eternal flames and stained all their posterity with the blood of that same innocent Jesus Christ, which, filled with diabolical fury, they stubbornly asked to be shed upon themselves and their children. Their indignation too was harsh and cursed, because, while it insulted Jesus Christ irreverently and insolently, it drew many after itself to eternal destruction. You too, wretched and pitiable Jews, will be cursed unless you drive the cursed fury of those same fathers from your hearts as soon as possible and believe without doubt that Jesus Christ is true God and true man and has already come. If, then, you wish to attain eternal joys, cast the obstinate fury of the Jewish rulers from your hearts, and receive with devout minds through the ministers of the holy Church the baptism of Christ, without which no one can be saved. May the harsh indignation of the scribes and Pharisees likewise be far from your minds, so that, rooted and grounded in the faith and charity of Christ (Eph. III), you may deserve to be counted among the elect. And what shall I say to you, O Jews? Surely, if you assent to my most salutary counsels; if you give assent to my most equitable admonitions; if you place faith in my most just exhortations, then, all doubt removed, with Christ as your guide, you will be able to reach the brightness of the heavenly homeland. But if you remain in the wickedness [Col. 0252C] of your unbelief, you will by no means be able to be saved.

§ XVII.—

The veil of Moses laid over the hearts of the Jews does not permit them to understand the Law spiritually. Baptism is shown to have been prefigured from the book of Exodus: baptism grants remission of sins. The Law did not produce the perfect person; circumcision did not lead to perfection; the sins of the Jews were not consumed when the Law was given, and legal observances were ended by Christ’s death. From the testimony of the same book, Christ’s resurrection is shown. He cries out against the Jews’ hardness and their shameful rejection. Speaking indignantly, the patriarch Jacob said to his son Reuben. He goes on to explain why the blessed patriarch cursed with so severe a judgment the Israelite people that would be born from him.

What more do you say, O Jews? What do you answer, [Col. 0252D] or what do you object? This is both your answer and objection: that you do not wish to receive Christ’s baptism because God in the Law of Moses commanded his worshippers to be circumcised, not baptized. To this we answer: according to the judgment of the apostle Paul, if a law had been given that could give life—that is, that could bring its observers to eternal life—then righteousness would indeed come from the Law (Gal. III). But the Scripture of the Law shut up all things under sin, so that the promise of eternal blessedness might be given to believers not by circumcision but by faith in Jesus Christ—that is, to those baptized in the name of the holy Trinity. Therefore, if you wish happily to obtain the promises [Col. 0253A] which Jesus Christ himself, Lawgiver and Judge, promised to your fathers, believe that he is true God and true man, and receive his baptism with devout minds. Know for certain that unless you humbly submit yourselves to his baptism, you will never be admitted among the number of his elect. For because the holy Church faithfully sought him at the river Jordan, she deserved to find him there.

This, O Jews, is your answer: that throughout the whole course of the Old Testament you have never been able to find where baptism was prefigured. To this we reply in turn that the reason you have been unable to find Christ’s baptism prefigured by the patriarchs or foretold by the prophets is that the veil of Moses has been laid over your hearts, and therefore you understand the Law not spiritually but carnally. Although we could show that baptism was prefigured in many other places—in the figures of the patriarchs, the testimonies of the Law, and the most true proclamations of the prophets—we shall nevertheless carefully demonstrate how clearly it was prefigured in the book of Exodus, both to refute your false objection and to confirm our faith.

You should know, O Jews, that Moses, from his infancy, prefigured Jesus Christ, the Saviour of the world, in his deeds. Moses was therefore nourished in his father’s house for three months; after three months he was put out by his mother and placed on the bank of a river (Exod. II). So the carnal Synagogue, like a mother, [Col. 0253C] expelled Christ as a little child from its fellowship, because he seemed a child when he was seen in human form. [Note: [Col. 0253D] Isidore, *Questions on Exodus*, ch. 5.] Moses, then, was found on the riverbank; and the Lord, of whom Moses bore the type, is found by faithful peoples at the river Jordan—that is, at the water of baptism. Meanwhile Pharaoh’s daughter, descending to bathe in the river, took up the infant. The Church gathered from the Gentiles, desiring the sanctification of the saving washing, joyfully received Christ. Pharaoh’s daughter found Moses enclosed in a little vessel of *tibin*, [Note: [Col. 0253D] See Grialius’s note on the passage in Isidore.] which was made from many wild twigs; the Church found Christ hidden in the hearts of saints, who, woven together in the unity of charity from the members of many brethren, [Col. 0253D] were all made one body in Christ and, receiving him through the worship of holy observance, venerate him with the highest honor.

Recognize therefore, O Jews, that Christ’s baptism, through which remission of sins is granted to believers by the cooperating grace of the Holy Spirit, was not invented only by Christ and his disciples, as you falsely claim, but was also truly prefigured in the Old Testament by the figures of the patriarchs and the proclamations of the prophets. Baptism in the name of the holy Trinity, administered to faithful peoples by the ministers of the holy Church, grants remission of sins to those who receive it with devout minds, [Col. 0254A] opens the heavenly kingdom, and admits them to the blessedness of the heavenly homeland. Circumcision, however, brought no person to perfection; before Christ’s passion it opened the heavenly kingdom to no one, and admitted none of the patriarchs or prophets to the vision of heavenly peace. Thus the Law produced no perfect person, because it perfectly purified no one’s sins. And, O Jews, so that you may know that what we have said is true, we shall demonstrate it by the testimony of the book of Exodus.
