Further, by the height of the cross, to which the head is joined, is signified the expectation of heavenly recompense from the lofty justice of God, so that good works themselves may not be thought to be done for God’s earthly and temporal benefits, but rather for that which faith hopes from above, faith which works through love. By the length, moreover, through which the entire body is extended, patience itself is signified, [Col. 0304A] so that we may remain long-suffering. Hence those who endure are called long-suffering. By the depth of the wood, hidden in the earth and from which all visible and elevated things arise, are indicated the unsearchable judgments of God, through whose hidden will one person is called to share in so great a grace in one way, another in another.

If therefore you desire, O Jews, to attain eternal joys with the children of the holy Church, build an altar of earth for God the Father: that is, believe that the Word coeternal with him assumed true flesh without sin from an incorrupt Virgin, redeemed the world through the cross, rose from the dead on the third day, ascended to heaven on the fortieth day, sits at the right hand of God the Father, and will come on the last day to judge the living and the dead. [Col. 0304B] [Note: [Col. 0303D] Supply: “believe.”] Set in him the anchor of your faith as upon the strongest foundation; strive to offer through him sacrifices of devotion to God the Father from a pure heart and an unfeigned conscience (1 Tim. 1). Through him, who is the way, the truth, and the life (John 14), hasten, by right belief and good works, to attain eternal joys. For Jesus Christ, God and man, is the foundation of faith, above which no one can lay another (1 Cor. 3). He is also the way, the truth, and the life, because no one comes to God the Father except through him (John 14).

Therefore believe, O Jews, that he is one true God with God the Father and the Holy Spirit; through right belief love him above all things with the same Father and Holy Spirit; and take the greatest care to follow him by doing good works. Do not separate the Son from God the Father and the Holy Spirit, nor the Holy Spirit from the Father and the Son, because Father, Son, and Holy Spirit are by nature one true God. [Note: [Col. 0304D] *Sentences*, I, distinction 19, chapter “And thence.”] On account of their natural unity, the whole Father is in the Son and the Holy Spirit; likewise the whole Holy Spirit is in the Father and the Son. None of these is outside any of the others because of the unity of the divine essence. From this it is plainly understood that the Father is in the Son and the Son in the Father, because their essence is one. Hence Jesus Christ himself, God and man, says: “I am in the Father and the Father is in me” (ibid.). Yet the Father did not exist before the Son, nor before the Holy Spirit. For these three persons are coeternal with one another. Hence blessed Athanasius says [Note: [Col. 0304D] In the Creed circulated under his name.]:

> “In this Trinity, namely, which is God, nothing is earlier or later, nothing greater or less; but all three persons are coeternal with one another and coequal.”

Hence God Almighty himself, who is truly three in persons and one in Godhead, says through the prophet Isaiah:

> “Before me no God was formed, and after me there shall be none” (Isa. 43), “because every knee shall bend to me and every tongue shall confess” (Isa. 45).

At this point I ask you, O Jews, enemies of truth, who by an impious conspiracy maintain even to this day that Christ is not the true Son of God and was not always in God the Father, [Col. 0305A] but began in time: who uttered the aforesaid declaration—the Father or the Son? “Before me,” he says, “no God was formed, and after me there shall be none.” Who said this? Did God the Father say it, or God the Son? Say, then, who said it?

You answer, O Jews, that God the Father said this. You add that God Almighty uttered this statement about himself in order that we might plainly recognize that apart from him no other God ever was, is, or will be. We answer that there is indeed, as you say, one true Almighty God, apart from whom no other ever was, is, or will be. Yet he is three in persons and one in essence. Therefore, when God the Father says, “Before me no God was formed,” he plainly shows that he is the beginning [Col. 0305B] without beginning. But when he adds, “And after me there shall be none,” he plainly demonstrates that God the Word did not begin in time but was always coeternal with him. The Son, therefore, is always in the Father, always with the Father, always alongside the Father. The Father in the Son and the Son in the Father dwell eternally in one another.

At this point, therefore, I challenge and entreat you, O Jews, as has already been said, that you should not presumptuously and irreverently divide in your assertion or faith either the Father from the Son, or the Son from the Father, or the Holy Spirit from the Father and Son; rather, believe without doubt that these three persons are one true God.

This, indeed, is found prefigured in Exodus, where among other things Aaron the priest is recorded to have been told: “You shall not go up by steps to [Col. 0305C] my altar” (Exod. 20), that is, if by degrees you place the Father above the Son, or the Son above the Father, or the Holy Spirit above the Father and Son, you will by no means be able to come to me. [Note: [Col. 0305D] Isidore, *Questions on Exodus*, ch. 34.] It is as if God the Father more plainly said to every order of priests, both of the Old and of the New Testament: “If you set me, God the Father, above my coeternal and consubstantial Son Jesus Christ, or him above me, you can by no means please me. If you believe either that I am prior to him or that he is later than I, you will not have me favorable even through offerings and sacrifices.”

For this is what the Arian heretics do, who strive to divide the indivisible substance of God the Father, Son, and Holy Spirit. Therefore believe, O Jews, that Jesus Christ is the true Son of God the Father [Col. 0305D] and of the Virgin Mother; that he mercifully redeemed the world by his most precious blood; that by his most merciful death he rescued those believing in him from eternal death; that he rose from the dead; that he ascended to heaven before the eyes of his wondering disciples (Acts 1); that he now sits at the right hand of God the Father; and that, as has often been said, he will come from there to judge the living and the dead. If you truly give faith to these articles of the Catholic faith, you will without doubt be free from eternal condemnation. But if you still persist in the evil of your unbelief, you will be unable to be freed from the slavery of sin either in the present age or in the age to come.

[Col. 0306A]

§ XXII.—

He foretells from the sayings of Exodus the slavery of the Jews, and prefigures how they may depart from it: namely, by offering God first-fruits—that is, the beginnings of their wills—and tithes, that is, the completion of good works. From the sayings of the same book he shows how they may change their carnal way of life for the better. He further explains that the Son is the Father’s arm and hand, and the Holy Spirit God’s finger. He explains why Moses broke the tablets as he descended the mountain, and what the calf, its burning, grinding to powder, and the people’s drinking signify. He also prefigures that the Old Testament would not last long, but that the New, marked by the ten words, would endure forever; in that number the figure of the cross is expressed with great learning. Moreover, he states how the holy Church was prefigured by types and enigmas: first, in Moses’ address to the Lord when he spoke to the Lord about the rock; likewise, he prefigures that one should truly address him as a worshiper of Christ. Finally, he figures the blinding of Jewish unbelief in the veil placed over Moses. In the ark made by Moses in the wilderness he prefigures Christ’s Church, and in the things contained in it he foreshows Christ as true man. He admonishes sacred teachers continually to meditate upon Holy Scripture. He proves that the New Testament, established by God, supplies what was lacking in the Old. From the sayings of Moses and others, he makes known in a subtle manner, in figure, the harmony of the Testaments: so that what one foretold as coming in the future, the other shows fulfilled. Finally, from the same book he adds a figure relating to Christ the Redeemer, to his members, and to the holy Church. Where we speak of seven churches, he indicates that they are one. In the same way, in the specific diversity of the tabernacle’s composition, he figures the righteous and sinners. He figures the Evangelists building upon the foundation of the prophets. He foreshows the agreement of the two Testaments and the one Church of the elect who came before and those who followed. [Col. 0306C] Thus too the apostles and prophets are prefigured, though in different ways.

God Almighty was without doubt foretelling this slavery, whether to God or to sin, in the book of Exodus when he said through Moses to the children of Israel: “Whoever, being a Hebrew, gives himself into slavery shall serve six years; but in the seventh he shall go out free for nothing. If he gave himself into slavery having a wife, he shall go out with his wife. But if he is unwilling to leave slavery because of his wife and children, his ear shall be pierced with an awl, and he shall be a slave forever” (Exod. 21). [Note: [Col. 0306D] Isidore, ibid., ch. 35.]

I want you to know, O Jews, that this history in the book of Exodus can be understood not only of the present age but also of the future one; for, serving God during the six ages of this world, in the seventh—that is, in the eternal Sabbath—we shall be freed [Col. 0306D] from the slavery of corruption and the law of death. Hence the outstanding teacher Paul, desiring that we be freed from this slavery and joined to the liberty of the elect, said: “The expectation of the creation awaits the revelation of the sons of God” (Rom. 8). For creation itself, namely the Christian people renewed through baptism and devoted to Christ through faith and works, will be freed from the slavery of corruption into the liberty of the glory of the children of God (ibid.). Again, elsewhere he says: “The grace of God in Christ Jesus has freed me from the law of sin and death” (ibid.).

Therefore, in the seventh age—that is, in the future age—helped by God’s grace, we shall be free from the slavery of sin and the law of death, if, while we serve in this sixth [Col. 0307A] age, we have withdrawn from unlawful works and have in every way been subject to God. But if we are unwilling to leave this sixth age for freedom, but instead choose to remain in slavery with our wives and children—that is, with our flesh and its carnal works—if we neglect to put an end to sins and vices, our ear will be pierced as a testimony of slavery, because, with no one compelling us but by voluntary choice, we have delivered ourselves into slavery; and thus we shall be slaves of sin forever.

Let us therefore recall to mind once more this pronouncement of the Lord, O Jews, that we may more suitably urge you to receive the true faith. For he says: “If any Hebrew gives himself into slavery, [Col. 0307B] he shall serve six years; in the seventh he shall go out, if he wishes; but otherwise he shall be a slave forever” (Exod. 21). I want you to know, O Jews, that “Hebrew” is interpreted as “one who passes over.” You therefore, who by denying Christ have delivered yourselves into the devil’s slavery, must take care to pass over as swiftly as possible into true freedom by confessing that he is true God and man.

If you wish truly to be called and to be Hebrews, you must gladly pass over from the Old Testament to the New, from the ancient Law to the Gospel, from carnal ceremonies to the spiritual sacraments of ecclesiastical religion, from earth to heaven, and from the slavery of this sixth age to the freedom of eternal blessedness. But if you persist in the treachery of unbelief, your [Col. 0307C] ear will be pierced as a testimony of eternal condemnation, and you will be wholly excluded from the liberty of the glory of the children of God. Without doubt, therefore, you will die in slavery to sin unless you truly receive faith in the same God and man Jesus Christ. He himself plainly testified this to you, saying: “Unless you believe that I am, you shall die in your sins” (John 8), that is, in slavery to sin.

Wishing also to free you from this slavery and lead you to true liberty, he said to you among other things: “If you remain in my word, and my words remain in you” [Note: [Col. 0307D] The clause “and my words remain in you” is not from this chapter, but from chapter 15, verse 7, and perhaps has fallen in here through error.], “you will truly be my disciples, and you will know the truth, and the truth will set you free” (ibid.)—namely, in this present life from slavery to sin, and in the future from everlasting condemnation.

But let us hear what you answer to the foregoing: [Col. 0307D] “We are Abraham’s seed, and have never served anyone” (ibid.). Certainly, O Jews, your answer is full of boasting and falsehood. Did not Joseph’s hands serve in Egypt “in the basket” (Ps. 80), and his other brothers in brick and mud? Did not your fathers, even while they yet remained in the land of promise, pay tribute to Roman rulers, willingly or unwillingly? And you yourselves, O Jews, now scattered throughout the whole world, have you not been delivered into slavery to all the nations under heaven and do you not pay a tax from your heads? Recognize, therefore, that you lied [Col. 0308A] in your answer, you who boast that you are Abraham’s seed and say that you have never served anyone.

O foolish Jews! David the patriarch rightly prophesied of you, saying: “They sharpened their tongues like a serpent’s; the poison of asps is under their lips” (Ps. 139). Your tongues are indeed full of lying and deceit; and you have sharpened them like serpents while you say that Jesus Christ, Redeemer of the world, is not true God but mere man. The poison of asps—undoubtedly deadly and foul—also bubbles beneath your lips, while not only do you make yourselves slaves of sin by denying Christ, but by false and impious persuasions turn others aside from the path of right faith and consign them to eternal death. Truly, O unhappy [Col. 0308B] Jews, you do not enter the kingdom of heaven, nor do you permit others to enter (Matt. 23). Do you not know, wretches, that unless through this Son of God and the Virgin, whom until now you have denied with proud minds, you can by no means attain from slavery to sin to true freedom? He himself testified this to you, saying: “If the Son sets you free, you shall truly be free” (John 8). Free from what? Namely, from slavery to sin. From what sin? Namely, unbelief. No one is greater in guilt than one who denies Jesus Christ, God and man. For according to the declaration of blessed John the Evangelist, whoever denies the Son does not have the Father either (1 John 2). Therefore, without faith it is impossible for anyone to please God (Heb. 11).

[Col. 0308C] I urge you, therefore, O Jews, once the hardness of unbelief has been utterly torn from your hearts, to believe that Jesus Christ is the true Son of God the Father and the true Son of the Virgin Mother, so that, freed through him from the slavery of unbelief, you may attain the liberty of the children of God. For unless you are freed through him, you cannot be freed at all. Repent, therefore, of your past treacherous unbelief, so that you may receive from him forgiveness of sins and through him come to God the Father. Through him, render to God the Father with devout mind the first beginnings of good thought; offer the first-fruits of true confession; sacrifice the offerings of right action; so that, cleansed by tears, fasts, and offerings, you may deserve to be companions of God’s elect.

For this is what God Almighty himself, who is three in persons and one in essence, prefigured in the Old Testament when he spoke figuratively to the children of Israel:

> “Let the children of Israel offer to the Lord the first-fruits and tithes of all fruits” (Exod. 34).

As I have often testified to you, O Jews, the Old Testament must be understood not according to the letter but spiritually. [Note: [Col. 0308D] Isidore, *Questions on Exodus*, ch. 37.] Spiritually, then, the first-fruits of crops or of offspring [Note: [Col. 0308D] Ibid.: “firstborn.”] signify the beginnings of works, or good will itself, which precedes work, and which the Pelagian heretics offend against by attributing it to themselves. But when God commands that this good will be offered to him [Col. 0309A] by us, he indicates that it belongs to his grace. In bringing tithes to the Lord, moreover, the number ten signifies perfection, because counting increases up to that number. Therefore, just as by first-fruits we are commanded to refer the beginnings of our wills to God, so by tithes we are commanded to refer to him the completion of our works; for from him are granted to us both the beginning of good work and the accomplishment of our petition.

Therefore, as we said above, O Jews, take care to offer your first-fruits and tithes—that is, good will, true confession of right faith, and the completion of good works—to God the Father through Jesus Christ, so that it may not happen that you perish with the unbelieving, but that you may attain eternal joys with the faithful. Strive, therefore, to understand the Old Testament not carnally but spiritually. Receive the New Testament with devout mind, so that you may walk no longer in the oldness of the letter but in the newness of the spirit (Rom. 7). Change also your carnal way of life for the better; wash away the stains of a perverse life with tears, so that you may become fit for the gifts of divine grace. This, indeed, is what the Lord prefigured in the Old Testament when he figuratively said through Moses:

> “You shall exchange the firstborn of an ass for a sheep” (Exod. 13).

For here the ass signifies impurity, but the sheep innocence. To exchange the firstborn of an ass for a sheep is to turn the beginnings of an unclean life to the simplicity of innocence, so that after a sinner has done those things which the Lord rejects as unclean, he may henceforth perform those things which he may set as clean [Col. 0309C] in God’s sacrifice. [Note: [Col. 0309D] Isidore, manuscript reading.] What follows, “If you do not redeem it, it shall be killed,” means that every unclean thing liable to sins, unless changed for the better, will be slain by everlasting death.

Therefore change your life for the better, O Jews, by keeping the right faith and persisting in good works, so that you may rejoice without end with God’s elect. I should like to know, O Jews, whether, having now laid aside the treachery of unbelief, you believe Jesus Christ to be true God and true man, or whether you intend still to persist in your evil? You answer that you neither receive the New Testament nor believe Jesus Christ to have been true God. O unbelieving nation, O wicked and perverse nation! From this it is plainly [Col. 0309D] understood that you have always acted contentiously against the Lord and have always been disobedient to him.

For after he led you out of the land of Egypt with a mighty hand and caused you to cross the Red Sea dry-shod, you made yourselves an idol at Horeb; to the dishonor of Almighty God himself you worshiped it, danced before it with tambourines and cymbals, and moreover cried aloud: “These are your gods, Israel, who led you out of the land of Egypt” (Exod. 32). You worshiped a mute and deaf idol more devoutly than Almighty God, [Col. 0310A] who rescued you from Pharaoh’s hand with great signs and wonders. You are therefore more senseless and foolish than all nations, you who, abandoning the true and ever-living God, rendered to idols the worship due to God not only in the wilderness but also in the land of promise.

Know with certainty, O Jews, and do not doubt at all, that Jesus Christ, whom in your proud minds you refused to believe to be the true Son of God, is himself the one through whom God the Father created all things from nothing, delivered the children of Israel from Egyptian slavery, gave them the Law on Mount Sinai, led them to the land of promise, and, having assumed humanity from an incorrupt Virgin, redeemed the world. For Jesus Christ himself is the arm and hand of Almighty God the Father. The Psalmist testifies to this, saying: [Col. 0310B] “He smote Egypt with their firstborn” (Ps. 135). With what did he smite it? Namely, “with a mighty hand and an uplifted arm” (ibid.), that is, with the Son.

Isaiah too, praising Jesus Christ himself, God and man, and declaring that he truly is the arm of Almighty God, says: “Lord,” [Note: [Col. 0309D] A passage conflated from two chapters of Isaiah: namely, 26:11, where the Vulgate has, “Lord, let your hand be exalted”; and 28:5, where it reads, “The Lord of hosts shall be a crown of glory”; and the Old Latin from Jerome: “The Lord Sabaoth, the crown of hope which is adorned with glory,” etc.] “your arm is exalted, God of Sabaoth, a crown of hope adorned with glory.”

That the right hand of God the Father, which is the Son, having struck Egypt and drowned Pharaoh, carried that same Hebrew people [Note: [Col. 0310D] Supply: “through.”] [Col. 0310B] across the Red Sea, is testified by the people themselves as soon as they emerged from the sea, singing a song to the Lord in great exultation: “Your right hand, O Lord, is glorified in strength; your right hand, O Lord, struck the enemy. And in the multitude of [Col. 0310C] your glory you cast down my adversaries” (Exod. 15).

So that you may not doubt, O Jews, that the Son of God is the hand of Almighty God the Father, I urge you to listen attentively to what the Israelite people adds again in the same song: “Who is like you among the mighty, O Lord? Who is like you, magnificent in holiness, terrible and praiseworthy, working wonders? You stretched out your hand, and the earth shall devour them” (ibid.), namely, the Egyptians.

Let us also recall the history of that time and hear together what it says of the hand of God the Father, which is Christ, through whom he freed your fathers from Pharaoh’s power:

> “It came to pass in the morning watch, and behold, the Lord, looking upon the camp of the Egyptians through the pillar of fire and cloud, destroyed their army, overturned the wheels of their chariots, and they were carried into the depths. And they saw the Egyptians dead upon the shore of the sea, and the great hand which the Lord had exercised against them” (Exod. 14).

[Col. 0310D] Therefore the Lord Jesus Christ is the most mighty arm and hand of God the Father; but the Holy Spirit is called the finger of God because of the distribution of gifts which are given in him to individual persons, as each has need (1 Cor. 12). You therefore inflict a great injury upon this same God and man Jesus Christ, who [Col. 0311A] mercifully rescued you from Egyptian slavery and powerfully brought you into the land of promise, while you are not only ungrateful for his benefits but also deny that he is true God and that he redeemed the world by his most precious blood.

We therefore prove that you have lied in your disputes, while we plainly show by most true arguments that he is true God and true man. But now let us hear together, O Jews, what Moses did when he descended from the mountain and heard the uproar of the people dancing before the idol. [Note: [Col. 0311D] Isidore, ibid., ch. 38.] Moses therefore descended from the mountain with the tablets; when he saw the people consecrated to idols, judging them unworthy to receive the Law, he threw the tablets from his hands and broke them at the foot of the mountain. After breaking them, he burned the calf that the people had made (Exod. 32). He broke the tablets which he had received written by the finger of God—that is, by the working of the Holy Spirit—because, as has been said, he judged the people unworthy to read them. But what does this calf which the children of Israel made in the wilderness mean, and what was signified by Moses’ burning that very calf, cutting it into tiny pieces, scattering it in water, and giving the people the water to drink?

It should be noted that in this passage Moses, descending from the mountain and crushing the calf into fragments [Note: [Col. 0311D] *Fragments.*], represented the Son of God descending from the bosom of the Father and destroying the devil, the inventor of all wickedness. For before Christ’s coming the human race rendered to God the worship due to him, and [Col. 0311C] worshipped him by the rite of a profane religion beneath the utterly vain inventions of idols. Therefore the calf is to be understood as the devil’s body—that is, the people among all nations whose head in sacrilege is the devil, their author. It was golden because idols appear to have been established, as it were, by wise persons. Of these the Apostle says: “Although they knew God, they did not glorify him as God or give him thanks, but became vain in their reasonings; and their foolish heart was darkened. Claiming to be wise, they became fools. And they changed the glory of the incorruptible God into the likeness of an image of corruptible man, and of birds, four-footed animals, and serpents” (Rom. I).

This, then, is the golden calf, whose images even the rulers of the Egyptians [Col. 0311D] were accustomed to worship as though they were learned men. By this calf was signified the entire body of the devil, that is, the whole association of Gentiles devoted to idolatry. The Lord Jesus Christ, descending from the mountain—that is, from heaven—burned this sacrilegious association with that fire of which he says in the Gospel: “I came to cast fire upon the earth; and what do I will, except that it should burn?” (Luke XII).

Moreover, it should be known that the Israelites, who at Moses’ command utterly ground down the calf and consumed it in drink, bore the figure of the holy apostles, evangelists, and other teachers of the holy Church. Thus that whole body—that is, [Col. 0312A] the entire gathering of Gentiles worshipping idols—is crushed: it is cut off and dissolved from the alloyed mass of that evil conspiracy by the word of Gospel truth; it is humbled; and, with the heart contritely broken unto wholesome repentance, it is cast into the water of baptism, so that the Israelites—that is, the preachers of the Gospel—may transfer it into their own members, that is, into the body of the Lord. For to the Israelites—that is, to the whole order of preachers—it was said in the apostle Peter: “Kill and eat” (Acts X). If he commanded them to kill and eat, why does he not also permit them to drink? For that calf was itself swallowed up by those whom it had tried to swallow, through the fire of heaven, the edge of the spiritual word, and the water of baptism.

Therefore believe without hesitation, O Jews, enemies of truth, that the Son of God descended from heaven and [Col. 0312B] assumed from the untouched Virgin a human nature without sin; that by his most precious blood he delivered the world from the devil’s power, utterly crushed idols, gave his elect a rule of spiritual life after the institution of the Old Testament, and called them to the freedom of the heavenly kingdom. Therefore, O Jews, you ought without hesitation to believe that Jesus Christ formerly put an end to the carnal ceremonies of the Law and established the New Testament unto perfection of life.

Moses also plainly prefigured that this same Old Testament would not remain for long. Receiving the first tablets from the Lord’s hand, he did not preserve them long, but immediately, descending from the mountain, [Col. 0312C] cast them from his hands and broke them [Note: [Col. 0312D] Isidore, *ibid.*, chap. 40.]. Those tablets, therefore, represented the ancient Law, which would cease not long after the people’s sin. But the other tablets, cut anew in the likeness of the first, bore the figure of the New Testament—a testament which we believe will remain in its established state until the end of the world. These tablets, then, were not broken, in order to show that the sacred sayings of the New Testament would endure until the end of the age.

For this reason the ten words of the Law were fittingly set forth on tablets, so that by that same number the figure of the cross might be expressed. For the letter *tau*, which is the twenty-second among the Hebrews, contains the number four hundred and signifies the New Testament, supported, as it were, by four columns—the four Gospels. Thus the form of the cross is inherent in the shape of the letter. For one straight stroke runs from top to bottom, while another, not unlike it, is formed crosswise as the arms. Hence Jesus Christ himself, God and man, says: “I came not to abolish the Law, but to fulfil it” (Matt. V), namely through the Passion, whose image was present in the tablets.

What do you say to this, O Jews? What do you answer, or what objection do you raise? I should like to know whether, having now laid aside the faithlessness of deadly obstinacy, you believe Jesus Christ to be true God and true man, or whether you still doubt in any respect concerning his divinity. For he himself instituted both the Old and the New Testament. He himself set the spiritual precepts of the New Testament above the legal ceremonies. He himself, [Col. 0313A] together with God the Father and the Holy Spirit, foreknew from eternity what should be fitting for each time.

In reply to this, O Jews, you tell us that you neither believe Jesus Christ to be true God nor wish to receive the New Testament. You add accordingly that you do not wish to receive baptism within the holy Church because you say that the Church itself was never prefigured throughout the entire sequence of the Old Testament. In response, we declare that Jesus Christ is the true Son of God the Father; that in the womb of Mary, ever Virgin, he espoused the holy Church to himself; that in his Passion he fulfilled the precepts of the Old Testament; and that thereafter he handed down to his faithful the commandments of the New Testament, to be observed steadfastly and beneficially.

The holy Church too [Col. 0313B] was foreshown from the beginning of the world in figures and mysteries: namely, in Adam’s rib, Abel’s righteousness, Noah’s ark, Abraham’s faith, barren Sarah, the construction of the tabernacle, the building of the temple, and the hearing and confession of the queen of the south; and it was prefigured in many other things. It was firmly founded by that same God and man, Jesus Christ; abundantly watered by spiritual doctrine; enriched by the heavenly gifts of the Holy Spirit; spread throughout the whole world by the holy apostles; blessed by God the Father; and most gloriously placed at the right hand of that same God the Father in Christ, who is its head and bridegroom. For thus Jesus Christ himself, judge of the living and the dead, will say when judgment has been completed: “Come, blessed of my Father; possess the kingdom prepared [Col. 0313C] for you from the foundation of the world” (Matt. XXV).

Therefore, to prove that you, O Jews, have lied in every respect in your objections, let us bring forward from the history of the book of Exodus how plainly the divine [Note: [Col. 0313D] *Voice.*] mystery of this same Son of God and man, Jesus Christ, and of the holy Church was prefigured.

For Moses says to the Lord: “Lord, if I have found grace before thee, show me thyself.” To him the Lord replied: “You cannot see my face. For no man shall see me and live” (Exod. XXXIII). As though he said more plainly: “No man can see me with the pure intention of the mind and the contemplation of a clean heart, and yet live in earthly and carnal love” [Note: [Col. 0314D] Isidore, *ibid.*, chap. 42.]. Whoever sees me with spiritual eyes immediately dies to [Col. 0313D] earthly vices.

Alternatively: “No man,” says the Lord, “shall see me and live.” Moses, representing here the elect of God, fittingly received the answer in the present life that he could not see the Lord’s face, because no human being could see it and live. For what does “You cannot see my face” mean except that, although human nature, even after the resurrection, advances to equality with the angels and rises tirelessly to contemplate God, it nevertheless cannot fully behold his essence? For not even angelic perfection itself attains complete knowledge, according to the Apostle, who says: “The peace of God surpasses every understanding” [Col. 0314A] (Phil. IV)—understand, even that of angels.

But let us hear what the divine voice, foreshadowing the mystery of Christ and the Church, says to Moses: “You cannot see my face; but when I have passed by, you shall see my back.” We believe that this meaning was fulfilled in the Gospel, namely when Moses and Elijah appeared speaking with Jesus Christ on the mountain (Matt. XVII). Thus he saw, at the time of Christ’s Incarnation, fulfilled the promise which he had received from God on Mount Sinai; for he beheld with spiritual eyes Christ’s “back”—that is, the things Christ performed in the latter and last days. Moses, as we have said, bore in this place the person of God’s elect.

But the Lord’s words to Moses—“There is [Col. 0314B] a place beside me, and you shall stand there upon the rock,” and shortly afterward, “I will remove my hand, and you shall see my back”—must be understood thus: Christ is seen only from the one catholic virgin mother, the Church, which he declares to be the sole one from whom he may be seen. Moses is therefore placed upon the rock so that from there he may contemplate some ray of the divine presence; for unless someone steadfastly holds the firmness of faith, he cannot in any way know the divine presence. Of this firmness the Lord says: “Upon this rock I will build my Church” (Matt. XVI).

Therefore, O Jews, enemies of truth, the sacred history of the Old Testament, spiritually understood, in showing beforehand that the holy Church was to be built in a future time upon Christ’s strength, openly refutes you in your dispute: you perversely assert that Jesus Christ, God and man, was neither prefigured in the Old Testament, nor has now come, nor redeemed the world. For this reason, at the time of his judgment, you will be for burning and food for fire, because you do not believe that he is true God and true man and has already redeemed the world by his most precious blood.

If, therefore, O Jews, you desire to attain the fellowship of God’s elect, you must, by faithfully believing in Christ, stand with Moses upon the rock—that is, upon the firmness of true faith. Place the anchor of your faith upon the firm rock, which is Christ, so that you may deserve not to perish with the unbelieving but to be companions with the children of the holy Church. [Col. 0314D] Believe without hesitation that Christ is true God and true man; receive the New Testament not falsely but truly; so that, renewed by holy baptism, you may walk not in the oldness of the letter but in the newness of the Spirit (Rom. VII).

What do you say to the foregoing, O Jews? What do you answer, or what do you oppose? I should like to know what your will is. This is your answer and objection, O Jews: you say that you neither seek to receive the New Testament, nor wish to be renewed by holy baptism, nor believe Jesus Christ to be true God; but that you desire only diligently to observe the carnal precepts of the Law given through Moses. O crooked and perverse nation, [Col. 0315A] impious nation, blind to behold the light of supreme truth, which is Christ! Do you not know that unless you are reborn and renewed from water and the Holy Spirit, you cannot enter the heavenly kingdom? (John III). Do you not know, O foolish nation, that unless you faithfully and firmly believe that the divine essence is three persons, you cannot in any way be joined to the assemblies of the faithful?

For the Lord plainly foretold this long blindness of your unbelief, O Jews, enemies of truth, when he said through the prophet of your rejection: “Bring forth the blind people who have eyes, and the deaf who have ears” (Isa. XLIII).

Moses also prefigured this blindness of your unbelief when he descended from the mountain [Col. 0315B] bearing a glorified face from companionship with God’s speech; yet, lest the children of Israel should be terrified and recoil from him in fear, he placed a veil over himself (Exod. XXXIV). Therefore, that we may explain more fully and completely what we have proposed, let us treat somewhat more broadly the history of that time [Note: [Col. 0315D] Isidore, *ibid.*, chap. 43.].

Thus, when Moses again descended from the mountain, his face appeared horned—that is, glorified—yet was covered with a veil. This signified that the same Law is covered with a mystical veil, hidden and concealed from unbelievers. For the speech of the sacred Law, if spiritually understood, has the hidden glory of knowledge; it has the horns of the two Testaments, armed with which it advances against doctrines of falsehood. When Moses is read, therefore, O Jews, Moses’ veil [Col. 0315C] is laid over your heart; consequently you cannot understand the Law’s mystical meanings. Because, through the excessive dullness of your hearts, you receive the Law and the prophets not spiritually but according to the letter, Moses’ whole face is covered with a certain veil, so that you cannot endure the glory of the speaking Law.

Know assuredly, then, and do not doubt at all, that if you do not believe Jesus Christ to be true God and do not wholly receive the New Testament instituted by him, Moses’ veil will never be removed from your hearts. The killing letter will be abolished, and the life-giving Spirit will be raised up. For God is Spirit (John IV; II Cor. III), and the Law is spiritual. Hence David prayed in the psalm, saying: “Unveil my eyes, and I shall consider the wonders of thy Law” [Col. 0315D] (Ps. CXVIII). As though he said plainly: “O Lord, unveil my eyes—that is, remove Moses’ veil from the eyes of my heart—so that I may be able to consider the wonders, namely the spiritual commandments, hidden in the letter of thy Law.”

For this reason, O Jews, I return so often to address and admonish you, because I desire you to be joined to the crowds of the faithful. Hear, therefore, what I say; hear what I warn; heed what I urge for your salvation. Already overcome by so many utterly certain arguments, and convicted by so many authorities of the Old and New Testament that Christ is true God and true man, you should long ago have driven the perversity of unbelief from your hearts and received the truth, which is Christ, [Col. 0316A] in the arms of true faith and love. If there were no one to explain to you spiritually the teachings of the holy Scriptures of the Old and New Testament, perhaps the guilt of unbelief would be less imputed to you. But now, because there is someone to explain them to you according to the rule of true faith, you have no excuse for your unbelief.

Believe, then, that Jesus Christ was sent by God the Father for the redemption of the world; that he assumed sinless flesh from an incorrupt Virgin; that he redeemed the human race through the cross; that he rose from the dead on the third day; that he chose disciples; and that through them he taught all nations the Gospel doctrine. Believe also that the holy catholic Church is the mother of all believers, and that no one can enter the heavenly homeland except [Col. 0316B] through it. For unless one confesses within the holy Church the faith of the holy Trinity, receives with devout mind from the ministers of that same holy Church baptism for the remission of sins, or pours out one’s own blood for faith in Christ, one cannot enter the gate of eternal life.

Persisting in the wickedness of your unbelief, you reply that you wish neither to believe in Christ, nor enter the holy Church, nor receive baptism, because you say that the same holy Church was never prefigured in the Old Testament. You also say that the Synagogue, instituted by God through Moses, is your mother, because through it [Col. 0316C] you think that you obtain forgiveness of sins and come to the heavenly homeland. In reply, O Jews, enemies of truth, we say that the holy Church was prefigured in many places in the Old Testament, as has often already been said, and that the future mother of all believers was foretold through the faith and operation of the supreme and indivisible Trinity. But through the Synagogue which you call your mother—that is, through circumcision, the carnal precepts of the Law, the traditions of the elders, Pharisaic superstitions, and superfluous bodily washings—no one could enter the heavenly kingdom, nor will you be able to do so.

Therefore, to strengthen our faith ever more and to confound your utterly false objection, O Jews, let us set forth from the history of the book of Exodus how the ark [Col. 0316D] which God commanded Moses to make in the wilderness prefigured the holy Church and its children.

“You shall make,” he says, “an ark of setim wood; you shall make above it a golden crown all around, and four golden rings, which you shall place at the four corners of the ark: two rings on one side and two on the other. You shall also make poles of setim wood and cover them with gold. You shall put them through the rings on the sides of the ark, so that it may be carried by them” (Exod. XXV) [Note: [Col. 0316D] Isidore, *ibid.*, chap. 44.].

By this ark, which Moses made at the Lord’s command from incorruptible wood, was signified the Church of Christ, which was to be built from all the saints who are incorrupt in [Col. 0317A] mind and body, and who also possess within them the two tablets of the Testament—that is, observance of the Law and of the Gospel. The ark was gilded inside and outside. So the holy Church ought to shine like gold, both inwardly with the splendor of life and outwardly with the brightness of doctrine and wisdom.

The golden crown all around and the four golden rings which were ordered to be attached signified that same holy Church, because, in being extended over the four regions of the world, it is without doubt proclaimed as girded with the four holy books of the Gospel. Yet these are enclosed within the circuit of one crown—that is, within the unity of the same faith. The poles are made of setim wood and inserted into these rings for carrying it, because strong and persevering teachers, like incorruptible [Col. 0317B] woods, must be sought: teachers who, always adhering to instruction—that is, to the doctrines of the sacred books—proclaim the unity of the holy Church and, as though through inserted rings, carry the ark. They are also commanded to be covered with gold, so that while they resound to others with the saving word, they themselves may shine with the splendor of life. Of them it is plainly added: “They shall always be in the rings and shall never be removed from them,” because those who keep watch over the office of preaching must necessarily not depart from the study of sacred reading [Note: [Col. 0317D] Gregory, *Pastoral Rule*, part II, chap. 11.].

For the poles are commanded always to remain in the rings so that, whenever opportunity or necessity requires the ark to be carried, no delay in carrying may arise from having to insert the poles. That is, when a subject asks a pastor something spiritual, it is very disgraceful [Col. 0317C] for him then to seek to learn when he ought to solve the question. Let the poles, therefore, always adhere to the rings, so that teachers, always meditating in their hearts upon the sacred sayings, may lift without delay the ark of the New Testament and immediately teach whatever is necessary. Hence the first shepherd of the Church fittingly warns the other shepherds, saying: “Sanctify the Lord Jesus Christ in your hearts, always ready to give an answer to everyone who asks you a reason for the hope and faith that is in you” (I Pet. III). As though he plainly said: that no delay may hinder the carrying of the ark—that is, the holy Church—the poles, namely the teachers, must never depart from the rings, namely from instruction in the four Gospels.

[Col. 0317D] As you see, O Jews, the aforesaid history of the Old Testament, spiritually expounded, plainly indicates that the holy Church was prefigured many generations beforehand, and shows beyond doubt that you have lied in your dispute. Therefore the Son of God, descending from heaven and assuming sinless flesh from the spotless Virgin Mary, put an end to the carnal ceremonies of the ancient Law; taught that the Old Testament must be spiritually understood; instituted the New Testament by his own and the Holy Spirit’s teaching, according to the will of God the Father; chose the holy Church, redeemed it with his own blood, and sufficiently instructed it by spiritual sacraments for attaining heavenly things.

Thus our Lord Jesus Christ is true God, possessing divinity by nature from God the Father; and he is true man, possessing true humanity from the Virgin Mother. In mercifully undergoing the Passion, he redeemed the human race from the dominion of the ancient enemy. Truly rising from the dead and ascending into heaven, made high priest for ever, he always intercedes with God the Father, in respect of his humanity, for all who obey him (Heb. VII). He is, in the present life, the spiritual medicine of the sick, the consolation and relief of the wretched; in the heavenly homeland, the sweetest fellowship [Note: [Col. 0317D] *Satisfaction.*] of angels and the eternal refreshment of all the saints.

And, O Jews, that you may know certainly and not doubt at all that what we say concerning Christ [Col. 0318B] is true, let us recall the aforesaid ark of the Old Testament, in order that, by spiritually expounding both it and the things stored within it, we may show beyond hesitation that Christ is true God and true man, and prove that you who persistently deny him even to this day have lied in every respect.

In that aforesaid ark of the Lord’s Testament there was a golden urn, the tablets of the Law, and Aaron’s rod which had budded [Note: [Col. 0318D] Isidore, *ibid.*, chap. 45.]. This ark, therefore, as we have said, is the catholic Church, possessing the two stone tablets of the twofold Testament, namely Old and New, and also possessing enduring stability. It also possesses the golden urn, which prefigured the pure and sincere flesh of Christ. That flesh preserves within itself the manna hidden [Col. 0318C] there—the manna of everlasting divinity—which is truly the sweet refreshment of angels and the perpetual delight of all saints. It also possesses Aaron’s rod: that is, the saving standard of immortality of our supreme and true high priest, Jesus Christ, ever budding with the unfading greenness of remembrance [Note: [Col. 0318D] “immortal.”].

Therefore our Lord Jesus Christ is true God and true man; he is high priest of high priests, King of kings and Lord of lords; he is mediator of God and men. In answer to this, O unhappy Jews, full of the malice, deceit, and fraud of unbelief, you say that Jesus Christ was not true God but a mere man, that he cannot grant forgiveness of sins to those who ask him, nor open heaven to those who believe in him. You further say that you do not wish to receive the New Testament because you know that it was superstitiously instituted not by almighty God but by Christ, who was a mere man.

In reply, O Jews, we say that, with God’s help and command, we can readily disprove these objections of yours by the authority of the Old Testament. For you are full of deceit and fraud; consequently all that you irreverently object against Christ and against the catholic faith is false. Our Lord Jesus Christ is indeed true God and true man, through whom God the Father created all things from nothing. He also has power to forgive [Col. 0319A] the sins of his faithful, because in the flesh which he assumed without sin from the incorrupt Virgin he offered himself to God the Father upon the altar of the cross. “For he died for our sins and rose again for our justification” (Rom. IV). As has been said, he has power to forgive the sins of his faithful, because in that flesh in which he suffered and rose again he always appears before the face of God the Father, pleading for them.

But when you say that you do not wish to receive the New Testament because you know it was instituted by Christ, you stray very far from the straight path; for you cannot attain the blessedness of the heavenly homeland except through him who is “the way, the truth, and the life” (John XIV). Truly he, Son of God and of the Virgin, is the institutor [Col. 0319B] of the New and Old Testament. Yet he placed the New Testament above the Old Testament, because he came not to abolish the Law but to fulfil it (Matt. V). For the New Testament is the completion of the Old Testament. And the Old Testament, if rationally understood and spiritually and faithfully observed, proceeds in harmony with the New Testament.

Therefore, O Jews, to show that what we have stated is undoubtedly true and to prove that you have lied in every respect in the aforesaid objections, it is necessary to bring forward the history of the Old Testament. For we shall never be able to defeat you better than by producing testimonies from your own books by which we may plainly prove ourselves to be false witnesses. Thus, to confirm our faith in every [Col. 0319C] respect and utterly convict your unbelief, let us hear what the divine voice says figuratively to Moses concerning the Incarnation of Christ and the harmony of the Old and New Testament.

“You shall make,” he says, “a mercy-seat of the purest gold: its length shall be two and a half cubits, and its breadth a cubit and a half. You shall also make two golden cherubim, beaten out, on each side of the oracle. One cherub shall be on one side and the other on the other. Let them cover both sides of the mercy-seat, spreading their wings and covering the oracle; let them look toward one another, their faces turned toward the mercy-seat by which the ark, in which you shall place the testimony that I shall give you, is to be covered” (Exod. XXV).

What, then, is figured by the mercy-seat except the incarnate Lord, of whom the evangelist says: “He is the propitiation for our sins” (I John II)? Therefore the mercy-seat placed above the ark of the Testament signifies Christ himself, who stands between God and man as the mediating propitiator. Again the Apostle says of him: “God set him forth as a propitiation through faith in his blood” (Rom. III) [Note: [Col. 0319D] Isidore, *ibid.*, chap. 46.]. This mercy-seat is placed above the ark, just as Christ is the head of the Church (Eph. V). At its right and left stand the two cherubim, which means “fullness of knowledge,” that is, love of God and neighbour, through which the Lord is shown. For no one can come to God except through love of God and neighbour [Col. 0320A] [Note: [Col. 0320D] Gregory, Homily 6 on Ezekiel].

What, then, are the two cherubim, called the fullness of knowledge, except the two Testaments? One stands at the right of the mercy-seat and the other at the left, because what the Old Testament began to promise prophetically concerning the Incarnation of our Redeemer, the New Testament now narrates as perfectly fulfilled. The two cherubim were made of the purest gold because both Testaments are written in pure and simple truth. They spread their wings and covered the oracle, because we, who are the oracle of almighty God, are protected from impending sins by the edification of sacred Scripture. When we attentively consider its teachings, we are veiled from the error of ignorance by its wings.

Each cherub looks toward the other, with faces turned toward the mercy-seat, because the two Testaments disagree in nothing and, as it were, hold their faces turned toward one another. For while one promises what the other openly shows, they see placed between them the mediator of God and men. The cherubim would turn their faces away from one another if one Testament promised what the other denied. But because they mutually speak the same thing in harmony, they direct themselves toward the mercy-seat so as to look upon one another. For what the Old Testament designated from afar through the figures of the patriarchs and the oracles of the prophets, the New Testament has manifestly presented.

Therefore, O Jews, enemies of truth, that you may believe beyond doubt that what we say is true, let us bring forward, from among the many things which we could adduce to show the harmony of the Old and New Testament, at least a few for the edification of the holy Church and the refutation of your objection. What does it mean that, while Adam sleeps, a rib is taken from his side, from which Eve is formed (Gen. II), except that, when Christ died upon the cross, the virgin mother Church, redeemed from the wound in his most sacred side, grew forth? What likewise does it mean that Isaac is led to be sacrificed, bears the wood, is laid upon the altar, and lives (Gen. XXII), except that our Redeemer, led to the Passion, himself bore the wood of his cross (John XIX), and thus died for us in sacrifice according to his humanity, yet remained immortal according to his divinity?

Thus the two Testaments agree in the mediator of God and men: what one foretold as yet to come in a future time, the other openly shows to have been fulfilled already. Therefore, O Jews, the aforesaid history of the Old Testament proclaims with certainty that Jesus Christ is mediator of God and men; and it openly declares you who deny him to be false witnesses in your assertion. According to his divinity, God the Father ineffably begot him from himself before all ages; the spotless Virgin, without a man’s embrace, bore him in time as true God and true man. He possesses divinity by nature from the essence of God the Father; he possesses [Col. 0321A] true human flesh by nature from the substance of the Virgin Mother. Therefore he is mediator of God and men. He is the medicine of the sick, the hope of the fallen, the way of those hastening toward the joys of eternal flourishing. He is the food and sweet refreshment of the blessed citizens of the heavenly homeland. For Jesus Christ, God and man, unceasingly guards and bears, governs and enlightens, and raises to the heavenly homeland the holy Church which he delivered from eternal damnation by his most precious blood.

Since, O Jews, you have already been refuted by the testimonies of the Law, the prophecies of the prophets, and the most certain proclamations of the evangelists concerning your assertions, you ought, putting aside all delay, to believe that Christ is true God and true man; that he redeemed the world through his Passion and cross; and that by his preaching he enlightened and enriched with the gifts of the Holy Spirit the Gentile people who sat in darkness and the shadow of death [Col. 0321B]. Let us hear, then, what you say, answer, or object. This is at once your answer and your objection, O Jews: you say that Jesus Christ was not true God but a mere man, and that he cannot redeem or guard the holy Church, or raise it with himself into heaven.

But we answer you in return that Jesus Christ is true God and true man. In that flesh which he assumed without sin from the Virgin, he joined the holy Church to himself; as we have said, he sufficiently instructed it with spiritual sacraments; purified it from sins by his sacred baptism; brought it to freedom by his Passion and resurrection; daily nourishes it with his most precious body and blood; most excellently ennobles it with the gifts of the Holy Spirit; unceasingly bears and governs it; and without interruption conveys it to the brightness of the heavenly homeland. Therefore, in order to show more clearly than light that what we have said concerning Christ and his Church [Note: [Col. 0321D] *Supply: “we have said,” or something similar.*] is true, and to prove that you have lied in every respect in your assertion before God and men, let us bring forward the testimony of the book of Exodus.

What, then, the Lord said to Moses, let us hear. “You shall make a lampstand of beaten work from the purest gold, its shaft and branches, cups, and little globes, and lilies proceeding from it” (Exod. 25). [Note: [Col. 0321D] Gregory, as cited above.] [Col. 0321D] What, then, is signified by the lampstand, O Jews, enemies of truth, except the Redeemer of the human race? For in him the nature of humanity shone with the light of divinity, so that he might become the lampstand of the world, and that every sinner might see, in his light, in what darkness he lay. Because he assumed our nature without fault, the lampstand of the tabernacle is commanded to be made of the purest gold. It is made by beating and drawing out; for our Redeemer, who from conception and birth is perfect God and perfect man, endured the bitterness of sufferings and thus came to the glory of the resurrection. Therefore Christ was a lampstand of beaten work from the purest gold [Col. 0322A], because he had no sin, yet his body advanced to immortality through suffering and reproaches. For, according to the merit of his soul, by which he might have advanced, he had no advancement at all; but in his members—which we are—he advances daily through blows, because, while we are struck and afflicted so that we may deserve to be his body, he himself advances. Of this body it is written: “From whom the whole body, supplied and built up through joints and connections, grows with the increase of God” (Col. 2). For all of us are his body.

Therefore the body is bound together through joints and connections: while the breast is joined to the head, the arms to the breast, the hands to the arms, the fingers to the hands, and the other limbs adhere to the limbs, [Col. 0322B] the whole body is made complete. Thus the holy apostles, because they stood close to our Redeemer, adhered to the head like the breast; and because martyrs followed them, they were like arms joined to the breast. When pastors and teachers are now joined to these through good works in the peace of the Church, the hands adhere to the arms. Thus this whole body of our Redeemer is daily supplied through joints and connections in heaven, because, when those chosen souls are led to him, his members are gathered to him. Hence it is well added: “supplied and built up, it grows with the increase of God”; because Jesus Christ our Redeemer, who has in himself nothing by which he may advance, nevertheless daily receives increase through his members. Hence it is again written: “Until we all attain to the measure of the age of the fullness of Christ” (Eph. 4).

The shaft of the same lampstand must be understood as that same holy Church, which is Christ’s body, because it stands free amid so many adversities. The branches proceeding from the shaft are the preachers of the holy Church, who send forth a sweet sound into the world: namely, the new song, that is, Christ’s new commandments, of which it is said [Note: [Col. 0322D] The cited words are also Gregory’s, but in Homily 32 on the Gospels]: “A new man came into the world; he gave new commandments to the world.” Cups are customarily filled with wine. What are the minds of teachers but cups, which intoxicate us with the wine of knowledge, so that we may forget the delights of this world which we loved? A little sphere rolls in every direction; and preaching which can neither be restrained by adversity [Col. 0322D] nor lifted up by prosperity is a little sphere, because it is strong amid adversity and humble amid prosperity, possessing neither the corner of fear nor that of exaltation. Thus it cannot be fixed in its course, because it moves itself in a rolling fashion through all things. To pursue the example which we have brought forward: lilies are fittingly described on the lampstand after the cups and little spheres, because after the spiritual intoxication and delight of preaching of which we have spoken follows that verdant country, which blooms with holy flowers—that is, with eternal souls. Cups and little spheres belong to labor; lilies belong to recompense.

Therefore the lampstand [Col. 0323A] of seven branches, O unhappy Jews, signifies—or prefigured, as will be said below—Christ bearing the seven Churches, which the sevenfold grace of the Holy Spirit illumines with flashing splendor. We speak of seven Churches although the holy catholic, that is universal, Church is one, in order to indicate that it is filled with the sevenfold Spirit. Of this Church its bridegroom, namely the Son of God and of the Virgin, says through Solomon in the Song of spiritual love [Note: [Col. 0323D] Gregory, on this passage of the Song of Songs]: “One is my dove, my perfect one; she is the only one of her mother, chosen by her who bore her” (Cant. 6). The grace of almighty God is our mother, which regenerated us, born for death, to eternal life. This grace chose one dove because it gathers only those who persevere in simplicity of life and do not depart from the unity of the holy [Col. 0323B] Church through heresies and schisms. For many believers, while they direct themselves toward him, unite themselves with one another by the one desire for Christ, and, having one heart and one soul, join themselves in charity, make one body from many members; and all who live in the simplicity of unity are one dove, that is, one catholic Church. She alone is called perfect and chosen by her mother, that is, divine grace, because outside this holy Church of which we have spoken no one can attain perfection or eternal life [Note: [Col. 0323D] Isidore, as cited above, ch. 49.]. Therefore the lampstand of seven branches, as was said, most clearly prefigured Jesus Christ bearing the sevenfold Church, enlightening and governing it, and leading it after himself to the heavenly homeland.

[Col. 0323C] Snuffers are made for this lampstand, which in the Law are called tongs. These snuffers of the lampstand are interpreted as the two Testaments, by which sins are cleansed and which are joined to one another by the union of the Holy Spirit. The lampstand is commanded to burn outside the veil of the testimony which is spread out, because the truth of the Holy Spirit now shines without any veil of the Old Testament. The oil which the Lord carefully commands to be offered from olive trees signifies the grace of the Holy Spirit, possessing peace and mercy in itself through the Savior’s coming; hence the light of truth is kindled also in our hearts.

Therefore the aforementioned testimony of the book of Exodus, O Jews, enemies of truth, openly proclaims that Christ was prefigured in the Old Testament [Col. 0323D], and plainly demonstrates that you who stubbornly deny that he has already come, redeemed the world by his most precious blood, and joined the holy Church to himself, are false witnesses. He has now come, sent by God the Father into this world; he firmly founded in himself—the foundation of true faith—the holy Church gathered from Jews and Gentiles; he builds it without ceasing from living and chosen stones; and daily raises it to the splendor of the heavenly homeland. Therefore, lest you doubt that what we say is true, [Col. 0324A] we wish to prove it from the construction of the tabernacle, which Moses built in the wilderness at the Lord’s command. I therefore warn you, O faithless Jews, to hear attentively how clearly the tabernacle which Moses built in the desert by the Lord’s command bore spiritually the figure of the holy Church, which you deny to be Christ’s bride and redeemed by him.

[Note: [Col. 0323D] Isidore, ibid., ch. 50.] This tabernacle, then, signified allegorically the holy Church established in the wilderness of this life. Of it the Psalmist says: “For he hid me in his tabernacle; in the day of evils he protected me in the secret place of his tabernacle” (Ps. 26). The tabernacle is constructed from various materials, some precious and some more ordinary, by which it is shown that there are both saints and sinners in the Church. [Col. 0324B] But let us hear again what the Lord says to Moses. “You shall make ten goat-hair coverings to cover the roof of the tabernacle. You shall make upon it another covering of red-dyed ram skins. You shall also make a third covering of twisted fine linen, hyacinth, purple, and twice-dyed scarlet, in embroidered work” [Note: [Col. 0324D] Gregory, *Morals*, book 25, ch. 16.].

What, then, do we understand by the ram skins and goat-hair coverings by which the tabernacle is covered, except certain ecclesiastical men devoted to secular concerns, who sometimes, by the hidden judgment of God, are set over others in the holy Church although they are harsh and strict? And because they do not fear to serve temporal concerns, they must endure the winds and rains of temptation arising from this world’s adversities. But what is signified by hyacinth and twice-dyed scarlet [Col. 0324C] except the inner life of subjects, illustrious in innocence and holiness? When this is carefully [Note: [Col. 0324D] “Carefully” (*caute*).] hidden in the tabernacle beneath goat hair and skins, its whole beauty is preserved: fine linen shines in the inner tabernacles, scarlet gleams, blue hyacinth glitters, while above them the skins and goat hair endure rain, winds, and dust. Therefore those who have advanced [Note: [Col. 0324D] “They advance” or “have advanced” (*proficiunt seu profecerint*).] in great virtues within the bosom of the holy Church ought not despise the lives of their superiors when they see them occupied with outward concerns. For their own secure access to inward things depends upon the assistance of those who labor outwardly against the storms of this age. What grace of its whiteness would fine linen retain if rain touched it? Or what brilliance and brightness would scarlet or hyacinth display if dust falling upon them defiled them? Let there therefore be above a strong goat-hair covering fit to withstand dust, and beneath it a hyacinthine color suited to beauty. Let those who devote themselves solely to spiritual pursuits adorn the holy Church; let those whom the labor of temporal affairs does not weigh down cover the Church. Therefore let not one who shines spiritually within the holy Church murmur against his ruler who deals with outward things. If you glow securely within as scarlet, why accuse the goat hair by which you are protected?

Thus, because the tabernacle [Col. 0325A] constructed in the wilderness at the Lord’s command so plainly prefigured, O unhappy—indeed, most unhappy—Jews, the holy Church and its ministers, namely the prelates and subjects who would be in it, it most clearly refutes you in your utterly false assertions, since you refuse to give faith either to the figures of the patriarchs, the prophecies of the prophets, or the proclamations of the apostles. To strengthen our faith ever more and to convict your faithlessness completely, let us bring forward from the utterly true history of that time how the whole construction and arrangement of the tabernacle, spiritually understood, prefigured beyond all doubt that same holy Church, mother of all Christians, and its ministers—the apostles, evangelists, and other teachers—as well as all the patriarchs and prophets who from the beginning [Col. 0325B] of the world foretold that Christ would come.

The Lord said to Moses: “You shall make four columns, their bases being cast in silver” (Exod. 26). [Note: [Col. 0325D] Isidore, ibid., ch. 51.] These four columns prefigured the four evangelists, to be established in Christ and in the Church by the firmness of faith. The bases of the columns are said to be silver, namely because of the brightness of the divine word. The bases of these columns therefore prefigured the saints of the Old Testament, who bear the structure of the Church by their support. For the evangelists are placed upon the foundation of the prophets, and confirm the evangelical faith by their authority. That these four columns had [Col. 0325C] gilded capitals prefigured him of whom the Apostle says: “Christ is the head of man” (1 Cor. 11). Thus, O Jews, enemies of truth, the Old and New Testaments evidently agree with one another, since prophets and evangelists affirm that Jesus Christ is true God and true man. The fathers of the Old and New Testaments meet in the one faith of Jesus Christ, mediator of God and men; and they show that you who deny him with obstinate mind have lied in your objections. The ancient fathers believed that they would be saved through Christ, whose coming they knew without doubt beforehand; but the fathers of the New Testament wholly trust that they will be saved through him whom they believe without doubt has already come and redeemed the world.

[Col. 0325D] Without doubt God and man Jesus Christ himself, through whom God the Father rules and orders all things, most certainly showed beforehand that this concord of the Old and New Testaments would come to be when, in the construction of the tabernacle, he commanded that silver columns stand inside, but that bronze pegs be driven outside all around, so that the tabernacle, fastened to them, might stand firmly. For thus the Lord says to Moses:

“You shall make pegs for the tabernacle and the court, with their cords” (Exod. 35). [Note: [Col. 0325D] Gregory, Homily 15 on Ezekiel.] The fathers of the Old Testament, because they stood farther off from the Incarnation of our Redeemer by the intervals of time, seemed, as it were, to stand outside. And because the suffering [Col. 0326A] of the Church began already with Abel’s blood, there is one Church of the elect who precede and follow. Yet because it is said to the disciples, “Many kings and prophets wished to see what you see and did not see it, and to hear what you hear and did not hear it” (Luke 10), to have stood, as it were, outside was for the ancient fathers not to have seen bodily the presence of our Redeemer. They were therefore outwardly placed, but not separated from the holy Church, because in mind, deed, and preaching they held these sacraments of faith already, as St. Gregory says [Note: [Col. 0326D] Rather, as cited above.] in the *Pastoral Rule*; they contemplated with spiritual eyes that height of the holy Church which we still await, yet already behold by possessing it. For as we are saved by faith in the past suffering of our Redeemer, so they were saved by faith in that same suffering yet to come. They were therefore outside, not outside the mystery but outside its time.

Hence, in the construction of the tabernacle, while silver columns were commanded to stand within, bronze pegs were commanded to be driven around outside, upon which the tabernacle was to be held by cords. The silver columns stand inside, while the bronze pegs are driven outside around them, and cords are tied to them so that the tabernacle may remain fixed. Thus, in order that the holy apostles might stand firm in the light of their preaching, and that the whole tabernacle—that is, the holy Church—might stand in the integrity of faith, the fathers of the Old Testament, namely the patriarchs and prophets, were fixed outside like bronze pegs, so that by the cords of their words they might bind the minds of preachers firmly and fasten this [Col. 0326C] tabernacle of God firmly in the state of true faith. The pegs are outside because they existed before the time of this holy Church; yet they bind those who are within it, namely the apostles and evangelists, because, in preaching heavenly mysteries yet to come, they made these things credible to all after they had been manifested. Thus, in order that the columns might stand immovable within, the pegs outside hold the cords; for the preaching of those who were able to see and preach the mystery of life before it occurred caused the holy apostles to believe it. Nor without reason were the columns made of silver and the pegs of bronze: for what the apostles now preach clearly, the prophets spoke obscurely under mystical understanding. Therefore the fathers of the Old Testament are rightly marked by the metal bronze [Col. 0326D], because they were not clear in their preaching. But the holy apostles, since they possessed the light of truth concerning the mystery of our Redeemer, are represented by silver columns.

And it should be noted that silver sounds and shines, whereas bronze sounds but does not shine. Thus the preachers of the New Testament openly spoke the things which they could also show; but the preachers of the Old Testament, because under the shadows of allegories they set forth obscure things concerning the heavenly mystery, gave forth sound as though without light. Therefore, O Jews, enemies of truth, the fathers of the Old and New Testaments agree without doubt in Jesus Christ, Redeemer of the world; and it is proved by the truest reasons that you who [Col. 0327A] stubbornly deny that he has come and is true God are false witnesses.

§ XXIII.—

When the sayings of the apostles are established by prophetic authority, he shows from the words of Exodus, spiritually understood, that what is said concerning the construction of the tabernacle figuratively represents the teachers of the New and Old Testaments laying the foundation of the holy Church; they build up and sustain the Church like bases and gilded boards. In the same place, he says that the goat-hair veils prefigure the future repentance of sinners, through which very many in the Old Testament pleased God; and he describes this repentance admirably from the words of Isidore. He proves, from the Jews’ own confession, that God alone can forgive sins, since he both inwardly enlightens the mind unto true contrition of heart and does not impute sins for punishment. For although Christ granted the Church the power of retaining and loosing sins [Col. 0327B], he alone, by the price of his blood, frees from inner stain and eternal punishment; this was not given even to priests of the New Law, as the Master of the *Sentences* declares in his own words. Peter, Paul, and John aptly agree with this truth, showing from the oracles of the prophets that we have redemption through his blood and that he is the propitiation for our sins. To these he adds Ambrose and Augustine.

I should like to know, O Jews, whether, now convicted by so many fitting figures of the patriarchs mentioned above, overcome by so many utterly true prophecies of the prophets, refuted by so many most brilliant proclamations of the evangelists, and shown false in your utterly false objections, you believe Jesus Christ to be true God, or whether, still hindered by blindness of mind, you doubt at all concerning his divinity coeternal with God the Father. This is your answer and at the same time your objection, O Jews. You say that our Lord Jesus Christ is not true God and cannot forgive sins to those who believe in him or lead them with himself to the heavenly homeland. We, replying to you, say conversely that Jesus Christ, mediator of God and men, possesses natural divinity from God the Father and true humanity from the Virgin Mother. God the Father ineffably begot him before all ages; the ever-Virgin Mary begot him in time from herself, made flesh without male desire. Therefore, because he is true God and true man, he possesses such dignity and power that he mercifully forgives sins to those who faithfully believe in him and humbly ask, [Col. 0327D] and causes them to adhere to him spiritually and to attain through himself—who is “the way, the truth, and the life” (John 14)—the heavenly homeland. Therefore, to prove that you have lied in every respect in your objection, let us bring forward testimony from the book of Exodus. When the Lord commanded the tabernacle to be constructed in the wilderness, I urge you, O rebellious and unbelieving Jews, to hear carefully what he commanded Moses among other things.

“You shall make ten curtains of twisted fine linen, and hyacinth, purple, and twice-dyed scarlet, in varied work and embroidered craftsmanship. Each shall be twenty-eight cubits in length and four in width. The same measure shall be for all the curtains. You shall make blue loops on the edge of one curtain at each side, and on the edge of the other curtain, so that the loops may meet one another and be joined together. You shall cast fifty golden rings to grasp the loops of the curtains, and the tabernacle shall become one. You shall also make eleven goat-hair coverings to cover the roof of the tabernacle. One covering shall be thirty cubits long and four cubits wide. You shall make fifty loops on the edge of one covering and another fifty on the edge of the other covering, so that they may join one another. You shall make fifty bronze clasps by which the roof may be fastened, so that one covering may be made from all the goat-hair coverings” (Exod. 26). As I have often affirmed, O Jews, the Old Testament is to be understood not literally but spiritually [Note: [Col. 0327D] Isidore, ibid., ch. 52.].

What we said above [Col. 0328B] concerning the columns, we understand also concerning the boards of the tabernacle and their bases. What then is signified allegorically by the boards, except the apostles, evangelists, and other teachers, extended through the whole world by preaching spread abroad? What is signified by the silver bases, except, as was said, the prophets, who support the boards set upon them, themselves firm and cast? For while the life of the apostles and evangelists is instructed by the preaching of those same prophets, it is made firm by their authority. Hence two bases are placed beneath every board, because, while the holy prophets agree in their preaching concerning the Incarnation of the Mediator, the apostles, evangelists, and other teachers who follow undoubtedly build the holy Church. And since they do not differ among themselves, they fix and strengthen those teachers more firmly in themselves. That he commanded the bases to be silver and the boards gilded shows that the commandments of the New Testament are far clearer than the precepts of the Law and the prophets.

Therefore patriarchs and prophets, apostles and evangelists, and the other teachers of the New and Old Testaments are represented by silver bases and gilded boards, upon whom the holy catholic Church is built. The Apostle testifies to this when he says to all the children of the same Church: “You are no longer strangers and sojourners, but fellow citizens of the saints and members of God’s household, built upon the foundation of the apostles and prophets, Christ Jesus himself being the chief cornerstone” (Eph. 2). Just as the teachers of the Old and New Testaments are signified by the silver bases [Col. 0328D] and gilded boards, so the remaining multitude of believers is figured by the tent-cloths, sewn with loops, suspended from rings, and tied together with cords, stretched out like curtains twenty-eight cubits long and four cubits wide. This multitude adheres to Christ and hangs from him by the cords of faith: “A threefold cord,” as Solomon says, “is not easily broken” (Eccl. 4).
